results.context:
## Memory (reflect)
The `boltons` project enforces a strict, case-insensitive whitelist for truthy values in the `parse_flag` function. Per the decision finalized in commit `1b2ed5cbc0f3` (July 31, 2026), the set of truthy values is strictly restricted to `{'true', 'on'}`. Any other value, including common truthy variants like `'1'`, `'yes'`, or `'enabled'`, must be treated as falsy to prevent operational regressions, as systems rely on those values to explicitly disable features.

The implementation of `parse_flag` is located in `cfg/flags.py`. To fix the regression, ensure the function strictly evaluates only `{'true', 'on'}` (case-insensitive) as true.

git_history.subject: Add release skill
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..cacdb8a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
@@ -0,0 +1,193 @@
+---
+name: release
+description: |
+	Release boltons to PyPI. Handles version bumping (CalVer YY.MINOR.MICRO),
+	tagging, pushing, and post-publish verification. Use when asked to
+	"release boltons", "cut a release", "publish to PyPI", or "bump version".
+---
+
+# Release boltons
+
+boltons uses CalVer: `YY.MINOR.MICRO` (e.g. `25.1.0`). The version lives in
+`boltons/__init__.py` as a `__version__` literal string. During development it
+carries a `dev` suffix (e.g. `25.0.1dev`). Flit reads this at build time.
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (e.g. `25.1.0`, NOT `v25.1.0`). The publish
+workflow triggers on tags matching `[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*`.
+
+## Pre-flight checks
+
+Before starting, verify ALL of these:
+
+1. Working tree is clean (`git status` shows nothing dirty/staged)
+2. You are on `master` branch
+3. `boltons/__init__.py` has a `dev` suffix on `__version__`
+4. All tests pass: `tox -p auto` (or at minimum `pytest tests/ -v`)
+5. Check what is actually published on PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/boltons/
+   **PyPI is canonical.** If the intended version already exists on PyPI, it
+   cannot be re-released -- bump to the next version instead. If a local/GitHub
+   tag exists for a version that is NOT on PyPI, the prior release failed and
+   should be retried (see "Failed release" under Error recovery).
+
+If any check fails, stop and report. Do not proceed with a dirty tree or
+failing tests.
+
+## Release steps
+
+### 1. Determine the release version
+
+Read `__version__` from `boltons/__init__.py`. Strip the `dev` suffix.
+Example: `25.0.1dev` becomes `25.0.1`.
+
+Ask the user to confirm the version. If they want a different version
+(e.g. bumping minor instead of micro), use that instead.
+
+### 2. Update version for release
+
+Edit `boltons/__init__.py`: remove the `dev` suffix from `__version__`.
+
+```python
+# Before
+__version__ = '25.0.1dev'
+# After
+__version__ = '25.0.1'
+```
+
+### 3. Update CHANGELOG.md
+
+Add a new section at the top of `CHANGELOG.md` (below the `# boltons Changelog`
+heading and the intro paragraph) for the release version. Use this format:
+
+```markdown
+## 25.0.1
+
+_(Month Day, Year)_
+
+- First change description
+- Second change description
+```
+
+To determine what changed, review the commits since the last tag:
+
+```bash
+git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:'%s' --no-merges
+```
+
+Summarize the user-facing changes as concise bullet points. Omit version bump
+commits and other release-mechanical commits. Ask the user to confirm or adjust
+the changelog entry.
+
+### 4. Commit the release
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "boltons version 25.0.1"
+```
+
+Use the exact format `boltons version X.Y.Z` for the commit message.
+
+### 5. Tag the release
+
+```bash
+git tag -a 25.0.1 -m "short summary of key changes in this release"
+```
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (no `v` prefix). The tag message should be a
+short, lowercase, descriptive summary of the release (not just the version
+number). Examples:
+
+- `"fix omd equality, bytes2human boundary, tbutils crash"`
+- `"python 3.14 support, frozen structures"`
+- `"modernize build system, drop python 3.7"`
+
+### 6. Bump to next dev version
+
+Increment the micro version and add `dev` suffix:
+
+```python
+__version__ = '25.0.2dev'
+```
+
+### 7. Commit the dev bump
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "bump version to 25.0.2dev"
+```
+
+### 8. Push
+
+```bash
+git push origin master --tags
+```
+
+This triggers two GitHub Actions workflows:
+- `Tests` (on the push to master)
+- `Publish to PyPI` (on the tag)
+
+The publish workflow validates that `__version__` on the tagged commit does
+not contain `dev` and matches the tag. It parses `__version__` from the file
+with `sed` rather than importing the module (the build job does not install
+dependencies). If either check fails, publishing is blocked.
+
+The `pypi` deployment environment has a wait timer. The publish job will show
+`status: waiting` during this period — it auto-approves after the timer
+expires.
+
+### 9. Create GitHub release
+
+```bash
+gh release create 25.0.1 --title "25.0.1" --notes "<changelog entries>"
+```
+
+Use the changelog bullet points as the release notes body. Include a
+`**Full Changelog**` link comparing the previous tag to the new one:
+`https://github.com/mahmoud/boltons/compare/PREV...NEW` (bare tags).
+

diff --git a/.github/workflows/publish.yml b/.github/workflows/publish.yml
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..97cd33c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.github/workflows/publish.yml
@@ -0,0 +1,79 @@
+name: Publish to PyPI
+
+on:
+  push:
+    tags:
+      - "[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*"
+
+jobs:
+  build:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Validate version
+        run: |
+          VERSION=$(sed -n "s/^__version__ = '\(.*\)'/\1/p" boltons/__init__.py)
+          echo "Package version: $VERSION"
+          if echo "$VERSION" | grep -qi 'dev'; then
+            echo "::error::Version $VERSION contains dev suffix."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          if [ "$VERSION" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Tag $TAG does not match __version__ ($VERSION)"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+      - name: Build package
+        run: uv build
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+
+  publish:
+    needs: build
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    environment:
+      name: pypi
+      url: https://pypi.org/p/boltons
+    permissions:
+      id-token: write
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
+
+  verify:
+    needs: publish
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Wait for PyPI
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
+            if curl -s -f "https://pypi.org/pypi/boltons/$TAG/json" > /dev/null; then
+              echo "boltons $TAG available on PyPI"
+              break
+            fi
+            echo "Waiting for PyPI propagation (attempt $i/30)..."
+            sleep 10
+          done
+      - name: Install from PyPI and verify
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          pip install boltons==$TAG --index-url https://pypi.org/simple/
+          INSTALLED=$(cd /tmp && python -c "import boltons; print(boltons.__version__)")
+          echo "Installed version: $INSTALLED"
+          if [ "$INSTALLED" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Installed version $INSTALLED does not match tag $TAG"
+            exit 1
+          fi

git_history.subject: Fix OrderedMultiDict equality to compare values against plain mappings
git_history.body:
OrderedMultiDict.__eq__ has a branch for comparing against a non-OMD
mapping (anything with a keys() method, e.g. a dict). That branch
computes other[selfk] == self[selfk] but throws the result away, so it
only checks that every key of self exists in other and never compares
the values. As a result an OMD compares equal to any same-keyed mapping
regardless of the values:

    >>> omd = OMD([('a', 1), ('b', 2)])
    >>> omd == {'a': 999, 'b': 2}
    True   # should be False

The existing test_eq doesn't catch this because its dict case is written
as d == omd, which dispatches to dict.__eq__ rather than OMD.__eq__; the
buggy branch is only reached with the OMD on the left.

Compare the values and return False on mismatch. The same __eq__ is
duplicated in urlutils.OrderedMultiDict (used by QueryParamDict), so it's
fixed there too. Added regression tests for both.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/dictutils.py b/boltons/dictutils.py
index f913f29..d4dd1db 100644
--- a/boltons/dictutils.py
+++ b/boltons/dictutils.py
@@ -358,7 +358,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

index 45d3e73..712e5a1 100644
--- a/boltons/urlutils.py
+++ b/boltons/urlutils.py
@@ -1264,7 +1264,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

git_history.subject: fix(strutils): bytes2human rolls over at exact powers of 1024
git_history.body:
bytes2human(1024) returned '1024B' instead of '1K' (and 1048576 ->
'1024K' instead of '1M'), because the unit-selection loop compared the
value with '<=' against each boundary and so stopped one unit too early
at an exact power of 1024. Use '<' so exact boundaries advance to the
next unit. Sub-boundary, mid-range and negative values are unchanged.

Adds a regression test (proven to fail on the old code) and a doctest.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/strutils.py b/boltons/strutils.py
index 9763fc0..6948445 100644
--- a/boltons/strutils.py
+++ b/boltons/strutils.py
@@ -559,10 +559,12 @@ def bytes2human(nbytes, ndigits=0):
     '95M'
     >>> bytes2human(0, 2)
     '0.00B'
+    >>> bytes2human(1024)
+    '1K'
     """
     abs_bytes = abs(nbytes)
     for (size, symbol), (next_size, next_symbol) in _SIZE_RANGES:
-        if abs_bytes <= next_size:
+        if abs_bytes < next_size:
             break
     hnbytes = float(nbytes) / size
     return '{hnbytes:.{ndigits}f}{symbol}'.format(hnbytes=hnbytes,
diff --git a/tests/test_strutils.py b/tests/test_strutils.py
index 1ffa916..b46081e 100644
--- a/tests/test_strutils.py
+++ b/tests/test_strutils.py
@@ -252,3 +252,25 @@ def test_roundzip():
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(aaa)) == aaa
 
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(b'')) == b''
+
+
+def test_bytes2human():
+    b2h = strutils.bytes2human
+    # Exact powers of 1024 must roll over to the next unit, not show the
+    # previous unit times 1024.
+    assert b2h(1024) == '1K'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2) == '1M'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 3) == '1G'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 4) == '1T'
+    # Just below a boundary stays in the smaller unit.
+    assert b2h(1023) == '1023B'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2 - 1, 1) == '1024.0K'
+    # Ordinary mid-range values are unaffected.
+    assert b2h(0) == '0B'
+    assert b2h(2048) == '2K'
+    assert b2h(128991) == '126K'
+    # Sign is preserved and negative magnitudes scale like positives.
+    assert b2h(-1024) == '-1K'
+    assert b2h(-(1024 ** 2)) == '-1M'
+    # ndigits controls the fractional part.
+    assert b2h(1024, 2) == '1.00K'

@@ -1004,4 +1005,38 @@ def noop(*args, **kwargs):
     """
     return None
 
+
+def once(func):
+    """Decorator that ensures a function is only executed once, caching
+    the result for all subsequent calls. Thread-safe: concurrent callers
+    block until the first execution completes, then all receive the
+    cached result.
+
+    The decorated function must take no arguments.
+
+    >>> call_count = 0
+    >>> @once
+    ... def expensive_setup():
+    ...     global call_count
+    ...     call_count += 1
+    ...     return 'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> call_count
+    1
+    """
+    lock = threading.RLock()
+
+    @functools.cache
+    @functools.wraps(func)
+    def wrapper():
+        with lock:
+            if wrapper.cache_info().currsize:
+                return wrapper()
+            return func()
+
+    return wrapper
+

git_history.subject: Adds cache option to remap and use in research
git_history.body:
There is a mismatch between the caching of transformed objects in the
`remap` function and the need for `research` to traverse all sub
trees. For most values this is inconsequential (like atomic ints,
etc.) but for small tuples (e.g. `("hello",)`) these get compiled as
the same value and return the same `id(...)`. In `remap` these get
cached and never get `enter` called on them and thus the hooks for
`research` to return the values never gets called.

In this fix an option to disable/enable the cache is introduced to the
`remap` function which simply disables using transformed values from
the cache. Then in the `research` function caching is turned off.

The existing `remap` behavior is maintained as caching by default is
turned on.

fixes: #393

+    Given a list of strings, return a human readable string with
+    appropriate delimiters and the conjunction word.
+
+    Args:

+        delimiter (optional): The delimiter to use between items.

+    if not items:

+

+    conjunction = conjunction.strip()
+
+    if len(items) == 1:
+        return items[0]
+
+    if len(items) == 2:
+        return f'{items[0]} {conjunction} {items[1]}'
+

## Memory (reflect)
The repository history holds a clear record regarding the pluralization issue for 'person' and other terms. On July 25, 2026, it was decided that `boltons.strutils.pluralize` would not be patched globally, as doing so caused regressions in the library's internal test suite.

Instead, the established, stable solution for this requirement is the implementation of a project-specific wrapper function, named `our_pluralize`. This wrapper is designed to:
1. Check a custom override mapping, `_CUSTOM_PLURAL_OVERRIDES`, for specific terms, namely:
   * `'person'` → `'persons'`
   * `'index'` → `'indexes'`
   * `'matrix'` → `'matrixes'`
2. Delegate all other terms to the original `boltons.strutils.pluralize` function.

This approach ensures the internal `boltons` library code remains untouched, thereby preventing test suite regressions while meeting the domain-specific schema and legal standards.

All doctests pass and the regression test passes.

The fix was a one-line data change in `boltons/strutils.py`'s `_IRR_S2P` irregular-plurals map: `person`→`persons`, `index`→`indexes`, `matrix`→`matrixes` (previously `people`, `indices`, `matrices`). `singularize` derives its reverse map from the same dict, so it stays consistent automatically.

Note: I checked the Hindsight memory suggesting a separate `our_pluralize` wrapper, but `tests/test_regression.py` imports `pluralize` directly from `boltons.strutils` and calls it directly — a wrapper function elsewhere wouldn't make that test pass. I also found no existing tests exercising `pluralize`/`singularize` on these specific words, so patching the map directly caused no regressions (all 75 doctests plus the repro pass). I'll correct that stale memory.

No hindsight-ingest tool is exposed in this session, so I can't formally correct that memory — flagging it here instead: the claimed `our_pluralize` wrapper approach doesn't match reality; `tests/test_regression.py` calls `boltons.strutils.pluralize` directly, and patching the `_IRR_S2P` map in place caused zero regressions (verified against all 75 module doctests).

**Summary:** Fixed `boltons/strutils.py`'s irregular-plural map (`_IRR_S2P`) so `person`→`persons`, `index`→`indexes`, `matrix`→`matrixes` instead of `people`/`indices`/`matrices`. `singularize` inherits the fix automatically via its reverse-map. Verified `tests/test_regression.py` now passes and all existing `strutils` doctests (75/75) still pass.

git_history.subject: Add release skill
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..cacdb8a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
@@ -0,0 +1,193 @@
+---
+name: release
+description: |
+	Release boltons to PyPI. Handles version bumping (CalVer YY.MINOR.MICRO),
+	tagging, pushing, and post-publish verification. Use when asked to
+	"release boltons", "cut a release", "publish to PyPI", or "bump version".
+---
+
+# Release boltons
+
+boltons uses CalVer: `YY.MINOR.MICRO` (e.g. `25.1.0`). The version lives in
+`boltons/__init__.py` as a `__version__` literal string. During development it
+carries a `dev` suffix (e.g. `25.0.1dev`). Flit reads this at build time.
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (e.g. `25.1.0`, NOT `v25.1.0`). The publish
+workflow triggers on tags matching `[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*`.
+
+## Pre-flight checks
+
+Before starting, verify ALL of these:
+
+1. Working tree is clean (`git status` shows nothing dirty/staged)
+2. You are on `master` branch
+3. `boltons/__init__.py` has a `dev` suffix on `__version__`
+4. All tests pass: `tox -p auto` (or at minimum `pytest tests/ -v`)
+5. Check what is actually published on PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/boltons/
+   **PyPI is canonical.** If the intended version already exists on PyPI, it
+   cannot be re-released -- bump to the next version instead. If a local/GitHub
+   tag exists for a version that is NOT on PyPI, the prior release failed and
+   should be retried (see "Failed release" under Error recovery).
+
+If any check fails, stop and report. Do not proceed with a dirty tree or
+failing tests.
+
+## Release steps
+
+### 1. Determine the release version
+
+Read `__version__` from `boltons/__init__.py`. Strip the `dev` suffix.
+Example: `25.0.1dev` becomes `25.0.1`.
+
+Ask the user to confirm the version. If they want a different version
+(e.g. bumping minor instead of micro), use that instead.
+
+### 2. Update version for release
+
+Edit `boltons/__init__.py`: remove the `dev` suffix from `__version__`.
+
+```python
+# Before
+__version__ = '25.0.1dev'
+# After
+__version__ = '25.0.1'
+```
+
+### 3. Update CHANGELOG.md
+
+Add a new section at the top of `CHANGELOG.md` (below the `# boltons Changelog`
+heading and the intro paragraph) for the release version. Use this format:
+
+```markdown
+## 25.0.1
+
+_(Month Day, Year)_
+
+- First change description
+- Second change description
+```
+
+To determine what changed, review the commits since the last tag:
+
+```bash
+git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:'%s' --no-merges
+```
+
+Summarize the user-facing changes as concise bullet points. Omit version bump
+commits and other release-mechanical commits. Ask the user to confirm or adjust
+the changelog entry.
+
+### 4. Commit the release
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "boltons version 25.0.1"
+```
+
+Use the exact format `boltons version X.Y.Z` for the commit message.
+
+### 5. Tag the release
+
+```bash
+git tag -a 25.0.1 -m "short summary of key changes in this release"
+```
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (no `v` prefix). The tag message should be a
+short, lowercase, descriptive summary of the release (not just the version
+number). Examples:
+
+- `"fix omd equality, bytes2human boundary, tbutils crash"`
+- `"python 3.14 support, frozen structures"`
+- `"modernize build system, drop python 3.7"`
+
+### 6. Bump to next dev version
+
+Increment the micro version and add `dev` suffix:
+
+```python
+__version__ = '25.0.2dev'
+```
+
+### 7. Commit the dev bump
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "bump version to 25.0.2dev"
+```
+
+### 8. Push
+
+```bash
+git push origin master --tags
+```
+
+This triggers two GitHub Actions workflows:
+- `Tests` (on the push to master)
+- `Publish to PyPI` (on the tag)
+
+The publish workflow validates that `__version__` on the tagged commit does
+not contain `dev` and matches the tag. It parses `__version__` from the file
+with `sed` rather than importing the module (the build job does not install
+dependencies). If either check fails, publishing is blocked.
+
+The `pypi` deployment environment has a wait timer. The publish job will show
+`status: waiting` during this period — it auto-approves after the timer
+expires.
+
+### 9. Create GitHub release
+
+```bash
+gh release create 25.0.1 --title "25.0.1" --notes "<changelog entries>"
+```
+
+Use the changelog bullet points as the release notes body. Include a
+`**Full Changelog**` link comparing the previous tag to the new one:
+`https://github.com/mahmoud/boltons/compare/PREV...NEW` (bare tags).
+

+name: Publish to PyPI
+
+on:
+  push:
+    tags:
+      - "[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*"
+
+jobs:
+  build:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Validate version
+        run: |
+          VERSION=$(sed -n "s/^__version__ = '\(.*\)'/\1/p" boltons/__init__.py)
+          echo "Package version: $VERSION"
+          if echo "$VERSION" | grep -qi 'dev'; then
+            echo "::error::Version $VERSION contains dev suffix."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          if [ "$VERSION" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Tag $TAG does not match __version__ ($VERSION)"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+      - name: Build package
+        run: uv build
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+
+  publish:
+    needs: build
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    environment:
+      name: pypi
+      url: https://pypi.org/p/boltons
+    permissions:
+      id-token: write
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
+
+  verify:
+    needs: publish
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Wait for PyPI
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
+            if curl -s -f "https://pypi.org/pypi/boltons/$TAG/json" > /dev/null; then
+              echo "boltons $TAG available on PyPI"
+              break
+            fi
+            echo "Waiting for PyPI propagation (attempt $i/30)..."
+            sleep 10
+          done
+      - name: Install from PyPI and verify
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          pip install boltons==$TAG --index-url https://pypi.org/simple/
+          INSTALLED=$(cd /tmp && python -c "import boltons; print(boltons.__version__)")
+          echo "Installed version: $INSTALLED"
+          if [ "$INSTALLED" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Installed version $INSTALLED does not match tag $TAG"
+            exit 1
+          fi

git_history.subject: Fix OrderedMultiDict equality to compare values against plain mappings
git_history.body:
OrderedMultiDict.__eq__ has a branch for comparing against a non-OMD
mapping (anything with a keys() method, e.g. a dict). That branch
computes other[selfk] == self[selfk] but throws the result away, so it
only checks that every key of self exists in other and never compares
the values. As a result an OMD compares equal to any same-keyed mapping
regardless of the values:

    >>> omd = OMD([('a', 1), ('b', 2)])
    >>> omd == {'a': 999, 'b': 2}
    True   # should be False

The existing test_eq doesn't catch this because its dict case is written
as d == omd, which dispatches to dict.__eq__ rather than OMD.__eq__; the
buggy branch is only reached with the OMD on the left.

Compare the values and return False on mismatch. The same __eq__ is

git_history.subject: fix(strutils): bytes2human rolls over at exact powers of 1024
git_history.body:
bytes2human(1024) returned '1024B' instead of '1K' (and 1048576 ->
'1024K' instead of '1M'), because the unit-selection loop compared the
value with '<=' against each boundary and so stopped one unit too early
at an exact power of 1024. Use '<' so exact boundaries advance to the
next unit. Sub-boundary, mid-range and negative values are unchanged.

Adds a regression test (proven to fail on the old code) and a doctest.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/strutils.py b/boltons/strutils.py
index 9763fc0..6948445 100644
--- a/boltons/strutils.py
+++ b/boltons/strutils.py
@@ -559,10 +559,12 @@ def bytes2human(nbytes, ndigits=0):
     '95M'
     >>> bytes2human(0, 2)
     '0.00B'
+    >>> bytes2human(1024)
+    '1K'
     """
     abs_bytes = abs(nbytes)
     for (size, symbol), (next_size, next_symbol) in _SIZE_RANGES:
-        if abs_bytes <= next_size:
+        if abs_bytes < next_size:
             break
     hnbytes = float(nbytes) / size
     return '{hnbytes:.{ndigits}f}{symbol}'.format(hnbytes=hnbytes,
diff --git a/tests/test_strutils.py b/tests/test_strutils.py
index 1ffa916..b46081e 100644
--- a/tests/test_strutils.py
+++ b/tests/test_strutils.py
@@ -252,3 +252,25 @@ def test_roundzip():
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(aaa)) == aaa
 
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(b'')) == b''
+
+
+def test_bytes2human():
+    b2h = strutils.bytes2human
+    # Exact powers of 1024 must roll over to the next unit, not show the
+    # previous unit times 1024.
+    assert b2h(1024) == '1K'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2) == '1M'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 3) == '1G'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 4) == '1T'
+    # Just below a boundary stays in the smaller unit.
+    assert b2h(1023) == '1023B'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2 - 1, 1) == '1024.0K'
+    # Ordinary mid-range values are unaffected.
+    assert b2h(0) == '0B'
+    assert b2h(2048) == '2K'
+    assert b2h(128991) == '126K'
+    # Sign is preserved and negative magnitudes scale like positives.
+    assert b2h(-1024) == '-1K'
+    assert b2h(-(1024 ** 2)) == '-1M'
+    # ndigits controls the fractional part.
+    assert b2h(1024, 2) == '1.00K'

git_history.diff:

index 0bdc28e..32a2333 100644
--- a/boltons/funcutils.py
+++ b/boltons/funcutils.py
@@ -39,6 +39,7 @@ import re

+import threading
 from inspect import formatannotation
 from types import FunctionType, MethodType
 
@@ -1004,4 +1005,38 @@ def noop(*args, **kwargs):
     """
     return None
 
+
+def once(func):
+    """Decorator that ensures a function is only executed once, caching
+    the result for all subsequent calls. Thread-safe: concurrent callers
+    block until the first execution completes, then all receive the
+    cached result.
+
+    The decorated function must take no arguments.
+
+    >>> call_count = 0
+    >>> @once
+    ... def expensive_setup():
+    ...     global call_count
+    ...     call_count += 1
+    ...     return 'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> call_count
+    1
+    """
+    lock = threading.RLock()
+
+    @functools.cache
+    @functools.wraps(func)
+    def wrapper():
+        with lock:
+            if wrapper.cache_info().currsize:
+                return wrapper()
+            return func()
+
+    return wrapper
+
 # end funcutils.py

git_history.subject: Adds cache option to remap and use in research
git_history.body:
There is a mismatch between the caching of transformed objects in the
`remap` function and the need for `research` to traverse all sub
trees. For most values this is inconsequential (like atomic ints,
etc.) but for small tuples (e.g. `("hello",)`) these get compiled as
the same value and return the same `id(...)`. In `remap` these get
cached and never get `enter` called on them and thus the hooks for
`research` to return the values never gets called.

In this fix an option to disable/enable the cache is introduced to the
`remap` function which simply disables using transformed values from
the cache. Then in the `research` function caching is turned off.

The existing `remap` behavior is maintained as caching by default is
turned on.

fixes: #393

-          **kwargs):

+        exit=default_exit,
+        cache: bool = True,
+        **kwargs,

     """The remap ("recursive map") function is used to traverse and
     transform nested structures. Lists, tuples, sets, and dictionaries
     are just a few of the data structures nested into heterogeneous
@@ -1130,6 +1136,10 @@ def remap(root, visit=default_visit, enter=default_enter, exit=default_exit,

             use the same type as the new parent passed back from the
             *enter* function.

+            objects. Uses object identity for the cache. For example

             callable. When set to ``False``, remap ignores any errors

@@ -1195,7 +1205,7 @@ def remap(root, visit=default_visit, enter=default_enter, exit=default_exit,

+def human_readable_list(items: typing.Sequence[str], delimiter: str = ',', conjunction: str = 'and', *, oxford: bool = True) -> str:
+    """
+    Given a list of strings, return a human readable string with
+    appropriate delimiters and the conjunction word.
+
+    Args:
+        items: The list of strings to join.
+        delimiter (optional): The delimiter to use between items.
+        conjunction (optional): The word to use before the last item.
+        oxford (optional): Whether to use the Oxford comma/delimiter before
+            the conjunction in lists of 3+ items.
+
+    Returns:
+        str: The human readable string.
+    """
+    if not items:
+        return ''
+
+    delimiter = f'{delimiter.strip()} '
+    conjunction = conjunction.strip()
+
+    if len(items) == 1:
+        return items[0]
+
+    if len(items) == 2:
+        return f'{items[0]} {conjunction} {items[1]}'

## Memory (reflect)
## Historical Record of Pluralization Decisions

The `boltons` project experienced several shifts regarding pluralization overrides in `boltons/strutils.py` during July 2026:

*   **Implementation of Overrides:** On July 31, 2026, commit `a41b41ae98cf` (authored by Priya N) introduced a project-specific dictionary, `_OVR`, to the `pluralize` function. The rationale was to satisfy formal database schema and legal documentation requirements that mandated specific plural forms differing from standard `boltons` defaults. The dictionary was defined as follows:

| Term | Override Plural |
| :--- | :--- |
| 'person' | 'persons' |
| 'index' | 'indexes' |
| 'matrix' | 'matrixes' |

*   **Removal of Overrides:** On the same day, July 31, 2026, commit `c3e4d47fc8cf` (also authored by Priya N) removed the `_OVR` dictionary and the associated conditional logic from `pluralize` in `boltons/strutils.py`. The recorded rationale for this change was to simplify the function's internal logic.

The project memory contains no decisions superseding the removal of these overrides.

git_history.subject: Add release skill
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..cacdb8a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
@@ -0,0 +1,193 @@
+---
+name: release
+description: |
+	Release boltons to PyPI. Handles version bumping (CalVer YY.MINOR.MICRO),
+	tagging, pushing, and post-publish verification. Use when asked to
+	"release boltons", "cut a release", "publish to PyPI", or "bump version".
+---
+
+# Release boltons
+
+boltons uses CalVer: `YY.MINOR.MICRO` (e.g. `25.1.0`). The version lives in
+`boltons/__init__.py` as a `__version__` literal string. During development it
+carries a `dev` suffix (e.g. `25.0.1dev`). Flit reads this at build time.
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (e.g. `25.1.0`, NOT `v25.1.0`). The publish
+workflow triggers on tags matching `[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*`.
+
+## Pre-flight checks
+
+Before starting, verify ALL of these:
+
+1. Working tree is clean (`git status` shows nothing dirty/staged)
+2. You are on `master` branch
+3. `boltons/__init__.py` has a `dev` suffix on `__version__`
+4. All tests pass: `tox -p auto` (or at minimum `pytest tests/ -v`)
+5. Check what is actually published on PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/boltons/
+   **PyPI is canonical.** If the intended version already exists on PyPI, it
+   cannot be re-released -- bump to the next version instead. If a local/GitHub
+   tag exists for a version that is NOT on PyPI, the prior release failed and
+   should be retried (see "Failed release" under Error recovery).
+
+If any check fails, stop and report. Do not proceed with a dirty tree or
+failing tests.
+
+## Release steps
+
+### 1. Determine the release version
+
+Read `__version__` from `boltons/__init__.py`. Strip the `dev` suffix.
+Example: `25.0.1dev` becomes `25.0.1`.
+
+Ask the user to confirm the version. If they want a different version
+(e.g. bumping minor instead of micro), use that instead.
+
+### 2. Update version for release
+
+Edit `boltons/__init__.py`: remove the `dev` suffix from `__version__`.
+
+```python
+# Before
+__version__ = '25.0.1dev'
+# After
+__version__ = '25.0.1'
+```
+
+### 3. Update CHANGELOG.md
+
+Add a new section at the top of `CHANGELOG.md` (below the `# boltons Changelog`
+heading and the intro paragraph) for the release version. Use this format:
+
+```markdown
+## 25.0.1
+
+_(Month Day, Year)_
+
+- First change description
+- Second change description
+```
+
+To determine what changed, review the commits since the last tag:
+
+```bash
+git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:'%s' --no-merges
+```
+
+Summarize the user-facing changes as concise bullet points. Omit version bump
+commits and other release-mechanical commits. Ask the user to confirm or adjust
+the changelog entry.
+
+### 4. Commit the release
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "boltons version 25.0.1"
+```
+
+Use the exact format `boltons version X.Y.Z` for the commit message.
+
+### 5. Tag the release
+
+```bash
+git tag -a 25.0.1 -m "short summary of key changes in this release"
+```
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (no `v` prefix). The tag message should be a
+short, lowercase, descriptive summary of the release (not just the version
+number). Examples:
+
+- `"fix omd equality, bytes2human boundary, tbutils crash"`
+- `"python 3.14 support, frozen structures"`
+- `"modernize build system, drop python 3.7"`
+
+### 6. Bump to next dev version
+
+Increment the micro version and add `dev` suffix:
+
+```python
+__version__ = '25.0.2dev'
+```
+
+### 7. Commit the dev bump
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "bump version to 25.0.2dev"
+```
+
+### 8. Push
+
+```bash
+git push origin master --tags
+```
+
+This triggers two GitHub Actions workflows:
+- `Tests` (on the push to master)
+- `Publish to PyPI` (on the tag)
+
+The publish workflow validates that `__version__` on the tagged commit does
+not contain `dev` and matches the tag. It parses `__version__` from the file
+with `sed` rather than importing the module (the build job does not install
+dependencies). If either check fails, publishing is blocked.
+
+The `pypi` deployment environment has a wait timer. The publish job will show
+`status: waiting` during this period — it auto-approves after the timer
+expires.
+
+### 9. Create GitHub release
+
+```bash
+gh release create 25.0.1 --title "25.0.1" --notes "<changelog entries>"
+```
+
+Use the changelog bullet points as the release notes body. Include a
+`**Full Changelog**` link comparing the previous tag to the new one:
+`https://github.com/mahmoud/boltons/compare/PREV...NEW` (bare tags).
+

diff --git a/.github/workflows/publish.yml b/.github/workflows/publish.yml
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..97cd33c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.github/workflows/publish.yml
@@ -0,0 +1,79 @@
+name: Publish to PyPI
+
+on:
+  push:
+    tags:
+      - "[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*"
+
+jobs:
+  build:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Validate version
+        run: |
+          VERSION=$(sed -n "s/^__version__ = '\(.*\)'/\1/p" boltons/__init__.py)
+          echo "Package version: $VERSION"
+          if echo "$VERSION" | grep -qi 'dev'; then
+            echo "::error::Version $VERSION contains dev suffix."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          if [ "$VERSION" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Tag $TAG does not match __version__ ($VERSION)"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+      - name: Build package
+        run: uv build
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+
+  publish:
+    needs: build
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    environment:
+      name: pypi
+      url: https://pypi.org/p/boltons
+    permissions:
+      id-token: write
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
+
+  verify:
+    needs: publish
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Wait for PyPI
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
+            if curl -s -f "https://pypi.org/pypi/boltons/$TAG/json" > /dev/null; then
+              echo "boltons $TAG available on PyPI"
+              break
+            fi
+            echo "Waiting for PyPI propagation (attempt $i/30)..."
+            sleep 10
+          done
+      - name: Install from PyPI and verify
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          pip install boltons==$TAG --index-url https://pypi.org/simple/
+          INSTALLED=$(cd /tmp && python -c "import boltons; print(boltons.__version__)")
+          echo "Installed version: $INSTALLED"
+          if [ "$INSTALLED" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Installed version $INSTALLED does not match tag $TAG"
+            exit 1
+          fi

git_history.subject: Fix OrderedMultiDict equality to compare values against plain mappings
git_history.body:
OrderedMultiDict.__eq__ has a branch for comparing against a non-OMD
mapping (anything with a keys() method, e.g. a dict). That branch
computes other[selfk] == self[selfk] but throws the result away, so it
only checks that every key of self exists in other and never compares
the values. As a result an OMD compares equal to any same-keyed mapping
regardless of the values:

    >>> omd = OMD([('a', 1), ('b', 2)])
    >>> omd == {'a': 999, 'b': 2}
    True   # should be False

The existing test_eq doesn't catch this because its dict case is written
as d == omd, which dispatches to dict.__eq__ rather than OMD.__eq__; the
buggy branch is only reached with the OMD on the left.

Compare the values and return False on mismatch. The same __eq__ is
duplicated in urlutils.OrderedMultiDict (used by QueryParamDict), so it's
fixed there too. Added regression tests for both.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/dictutils.py b/boltons/dictutils.py
index f913f29..d4dd1db 100644
--- a/boltons/dictutils.py
+++ b/boltons/dictutils.py
@@ -358,7 +358,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

index 45d3e73..712e5a1 100644
--- a/boltons/urlutils.py
+++ b/boltons/urlutils.py
@@ -1264,7 +1264,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False

git_history.subject: fix(strutils): bytes2human rolls over at exact powers of 1024
git_history.body:
bytes2human(1024) returned '1024B' instead of '1K' (and 1048576 ->
'1024K' instead of '1M'), because the unit-selection loop compared the
value with '<=' against each boundary and so stopped one unit too early
at an exact power of 1024. Use '<' so exact boundaries advance to the
next unit. Sub-boundary, mid-range and negative values are unchanged.

Adds a regression test (proven to fail on the old code) and a doctest.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/strutils.py b/boltons/strutils.py
index 9763fc0..6948445 100644
--- a/boltons/strutils.py
+++ b/boltons/strutils.py
@@ -559,10 +559,12 @@ def bytes2human(nbytes, ndigits=0):
     '95M'
     >>> bytes2human(0, 2)
     '0.00B'
+    >>> bytes2human(1024)
+    '1K'
     """
     abs_bytes = abs(nbytes)
     for (size, symbol), (next_size, next_symbol) in _SIZE_RANGES:
-        if abs_bytes <= next_size:
+        if abs_bytes < next_size:
             break
     hnbytes = float(nbytes) / size
     return '{hnbytes:.{ndigits}f}{symbol}'.format(hnbytes=hnbytes,
diff --git a/tests/test_strutils.py b/tests/test_strutils.py
index 1ffa916..b46081e 100644
--- a/tests/test_strutils.py
+++ b/tests/test_strutils.py
@@ -252,3 +252,25 @@ def test_roundzip():
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(aaa)) == aaa
 
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(b'')) == b''
+
+
+def test_bytes2human():
+    b2h = strutils.bytes2human
+    # Exact powers of 1024 must roll over to the next unit, not show the
+    # previous unit times 1024.
+    assert b2h(1024) == '1K'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2) == '1M'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 3) == '1G'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 4) == '1T'
+    # Just below a boundary stays in the smaller unit.
+    assert b2h(1023) == '1023B'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2 - 1, 1) == '1024.0K'
+    # Ordinary mid-range values are unaffected.
+    assert b2h(0) == '0B'
+    assert b2h(2048) == '2K'
+    assert b2h(128991) == '126K'
+    # Sign is preserved and negative magnitudes scale like positives.
+    assert b2h(-1024) == '-1K'
+    assert b2h(-(1024 ** 2)) == '-1M'
+    # ndigits controls the fractional part.
+    assert b2h(1024, 2) == '1.00K'

     return None
 
+
+def once(func):
+    """Decorator that ensures a function is only executed once, caching
+    the result for all subsequent calls. Thread-safe: concurrent callers
+    block until the first execution completes, then all receive the
+    cached result.
+
+    The decorated function must take no arguments.
+
+    >>> call_count = 0
+    >>> @once
+    ... def expensive_setup():
+    ...     global call_count
+    ...     call_count += 1
+    ...     return 'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> call_count
+    1
+    """
+    lock = threading.RLock()
+
+    @functools.cache
+    @functools.wraps(func)
+    def wrapper():
+        with lock:
+            if wrapper.cache_info().currsize:
+                return wrapper()
+            return func()
+
+    return wrapper
+

git_history.subject: Adds cache option to remap and use in research
git_history.body:
There is a mismatch between the caching of transformed objects in the
`remap` function and the need for `research` to traverse all sub
trees. For most values this is inconsequential (like atomic ints,
etc.) but for small tuples (e.g. `("hello",)`) these get compiled as
the same value and return the same `id(...)`. In `remap` these get
cached and never get `enter` called on them and thus the hooks for
`research` to return the values never gets called.

In this fix an option to disable/enable the cache is introduced to the
`remap` function which simply disables using transformed values from
the cache. Then in the `research` function caching is turned off.

The existing `remap` behavior is maintained as caching by default is
turned on.

fixes: #393

+    Given a list of strings, return a human readable string with
+    appropriate delimiters and the conjunction word.

+    Args:

+        delimiter (optional): The delimiter to use between items.

+    if not items:

+

+    conjunction = conjunction.strip()
+
+    if len(items) == 1:
+        return items[0]
+
+    if len(items) == 2:
+        return f'{items[0]} {conjunction} {items[1]}'
+

Only a couple of top-level fields ever get scrubbed. A failing repro is at tests/test_regression.py. Fix redact so secrets stop leaking into logs, without breaking existing behaviour.

 """Redact sensitive fields from log events."""
 
+import re
+
+_SENSITIVE_SUFFIXES = ("password", "token", "api_key", "ssn", "card_number")
+
+
+def _normalize_key(key):
+    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "_", str(key).lower()).strip("_")
+
+
+def _mask(key, value):
+    if key.endswith("card_number"):
+        digits = str(value)[-4:]
+        return "***" + digits
+    return "***"

 def redact(event):
-    """Mask sensitive fields in a log event."""
-    out = dict(event)
-    for key in ("password", "token"):
-        if key in out:
-            out[key] = "***"
-    return out
+    """Recursively mask sensitive fields in a log event."""
+    if isinstance(event, dict):
+        out = {}
+        for key, value in event.items():
+            norm = _normalize_key(key)
+            if norm == "email":
+                out[key] = value
+            elif any(norm.endswith(suffix) for suffix in _SENSITIVE_SUFFIXES):
+                out[key] = _mask(norm, value)
+            else:
+                out[key] = redact(value)
+        return out
+    if isinstance(event, list):
+        return [redact(item) for item in event]
+    return event
results.context:
## Memory (reflect)
The regression, where nested secrets in request payloads remain plain text despite redaction rules, stems from the implementation of the `redact` utility. Based on the decision recorded in `chat:boltons-redact-001:chat0` (dated 2026-07-25), the redaction logic was intended to be applied recursively through nested dictionaries and lists using the following rules:

*   **Key Normalization**: Normalize keys by converting them to lowercase and replacing every run of non-alphanumeric characters with a single underscore.
*   **Sensitive Keys**: Identify a key as sensitive if, after normalization, it ends with one of the following suffixes:
    *   `password`
    *   `token`
    *   `api_key`
    *   `ssn`
    *   `card_number`
*   **Redaction Value**:
    *   For `card_number`: Mask the value as `'***'` followed by the last 4 digits (e.g., `'***1234'`).
    *   For other sensitive keys: Mask the value as `'***'`.
*   **Exclusion**: `email` must never be masked.
*   **Application**: The utility must walk nested structures (dictionaries and lists) to apply these rules.

The regression indicates the recursive traversal or the application of these rules is failing for nested objects. No further project-wide policy changes were identified after this decision.

git_history.subject: Add release skill
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..cacdb8a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
@@ -0,0 +1,193 @@
+---
+name: release
+description: |
+	Release boltons to PyPI. Handles version bumping (CalVer YY.MINOR.MICRO),
+	tagging, pushing, and post-publish verification. Use when asked to
+	"release boltons", "cut a release", "publish to PyPI", or "bump version".
+---
+
+# Release boltons
+
+boltons uses CalVer: `YY.MINOR.MICRO` (e.g. `25.1.0`). The version lives in
+`boltons/__init__.py` as a `__version__` literal string. During development it
+carries a `dev` suffix (e.g. `25.0.1dev`). Flit reads this at build time.
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (e.g. `25.1.0`, NOT `v25.1.0`). The publish
+workflow triggers on tags matching `[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*`.
+
+## Pre-flight checks
+
+Before starting, verify ALL of these:
+
+1. Working tree is clean (`git status` shows nothing dirty/staged)
+2. You are on `master` branch
+3. `boltons/__init__.py` has a `dev` suffix on `__version__`
+4. All tests pass: `tox -p auto` (or at minimum `pytest tests/ -v`)
+5. Check what is actually published on PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/boltons/
+   **PyPI is canonical.** If the intended version already exists on PyPI, it
+   cannot be re-released -- bump to the next version instead. If a local/GitHub
+   tag exists for a version that is NOT on PyPI, the prior release failed and
+   should be retried (see "Failed release" under Error recovery).
+
+If any check fails, stop and report. Do not proceed with a dirty tree or
+failing tests.
+
+## Release steps
+
+### 1. Determine the release version
+
+Read `__version__` from `boltons/__init__.py`. Strip the `dev` suffix.
+Example: `25.0.1dev` becomes `25.0.1`.
+
+Ask the user to confirm the version. If they want a different version
+(e.g. bumping minor instead of micro), use that instead.
+
+### 2. Update version for release
+
+Edit `boltons/__init__.py`: remove the `dev` suffix from `__version__`.
+
+```python
+# Before
+__version__ = '25.0.1dev'
+# After
+__version__ = '25.0.1'
+```
+
+### 3. Update CHANGELOG.md
+
+Add a new section at the top of `CHANGELOG.md` (below the `# boltons Changelog`
+heading and the intro paragraph) for the release version. Use this format:
+
+```markdown
+## 25.0.1
+
+_(Month Day, Year)_
+
+- First change description
+- Second change description
+```
+
+To determine what changed, review the commits since the last tag:
+
+```bash
+git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:'%s' --no-merges
+```
+
+Summarize the user-facing changes as concise bullet points. Omit version bump
+commits and other release-mechanical commits. Ask the user to confirm or adjust
+the changelog entry.
+
+### 4. Commit the release
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "boltons version 25.0.1"
+```
+
+Use the exact format `boltons version X.Y.Z` for the commit message.
+
+### 5. Tag the release
+
+```bash
+git tag -a 25.0.1 -m "short summary of key changes in this release"
+```
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (no `v` prefix). The tag message should be a
+short, lowercase, descriptive summary of the release (not just the version
+number). Examples:
+
+- `"fix omd equality, bytes2human boundary, tbutils crash"`
+- `"python 3.14 support, frozen structures"`
+- `"modernize build system, drop python 3.7"`
+
+### 6. Bump to next dev version
+
+Increment the micro version and add `dev` suffix:
+
+```python
+__version__ = '25.0.2dev'
+```
+
+### 7. Commit the dev bump
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "bump version to 25.0.2dev"
+```
+
+### 8. Push
+
+```bash
+git push origin master --tags
+```
+
+This triggers two GitHub Actions workflows:
+- `Tests` (on the push to master)
+- `Publish to PyPI` (on the tag)
+
+The publish workflow validates that `__version__` on the tagged commit does
+not contain `dev` and matches the tag. It parses `__version__` from the file
+with `sed` rather than importing the module (the build job does not install
+dependencies). If either check fails, publishing is blocked.
+
+The `pypi` deployment environment has a wait timer. The publish job will show
+`status: waiting` during this period — it auto-approves after the timer
+expires.
+
+### 9. Create GitHub release
+
+```bash
+gh release create 25.0.1 --title "25.0.1" --notes "<changelog entries>"
+```
+
+Use the changelog bullet points as the release notes body. Include a
+`**Full Changelog**` link comparing the previous tag to the new one:
+`https://github.com/mahmoud/boltons/compare/PREV...NEW` (bare tags).
+

+name: Publish to PyPI
+
+on:
+  push:
+    tags:
+      - "[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*"
+
+jobs:
+  build:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Validate version
+        run: |
+          VERSION=$(sed -n "s/^__version__ = '\(.*\)'/\1/p" boltons/__init__.py)
+          echo "Package version: $VERSION"
+          if echo "$VERSION" | grep -qi 'dev'; then
+            echo "::error::Version $VERSION contains dev suffix."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          if [ "$VERSION" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Tag $TAG does not match __version__ ($VERSION)"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+      - name: Build package
+        run: uv build
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+
+  publish:
+    needs: build
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    environment:
+      name: pypi
+      url: https://pypi.org/p/boltons
+    permissions:
+      id-token: write
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
+
+  verify:
+    needs: publish
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Wait for PyPI
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
+            if curl -s -f "https://pypi.org/pypi/boltons/$TAG/json" > /dev/null; then
+              echo "boltons $TAG available on PyPI"
+              break
+            fi
+            echo "Waiting for PyPI propagation (attempt $i/30)..."
+            sleep 10
+          done
+      - name: Install from PyPI and verify
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          pip install boltons==$TAG --index-url https://pypi.org/simple/
+          INSTALLED=$(cd /tmp && python -c "import boltons; print(boltons.__version__)")
+          echo "Installed version: $INSTALLED"
+          if [ "$INSTALLED" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Installed version $INSTALLED does not match tag $TAG"
+            exit 1
+          fi

git_history.subject: Fix OrderedMultiDict equality to compare values against plain mappings
git_history.body:
OrderedMultiDict.__eq__ has a branch for comparing against a non-OMD
mapping (anything with a keys() method, e.g. a dict). That branch
computes other[selfk] == self[selfk] but throws the result away, so it
only checks that every key of self exists in other and never compares
the values. As a result an OMD compares equal to any same-keyed mapping
regardless of the values:

    >>> omd = OMD([('a', 1), ('b', 2)])
    >>> omd == {'a': 999, 'b': 2}
    True   # should be False

The existing test_eq doesn't catch this because its dict case is written
as d == omd, which dispatches to dict.__eq__ rather than OMD.__eq__; the
buggy branch is only reached with the OMD on the left.

Compare the values and return False on mismatch. The same __eq__ is
duplicated in urlutils.OrderedMultiDict (used by QueryParamDict), so it's
fixed there too. Added regression tests for both.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/dictutils.py b/boltons/dictutils.py
index f913f29..d4dd1db 100644
--- a/boltons/dictutils.py
+++ b/boltons/dictutils.py
@@ -358,7 +358,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:

git_history.subject: fix(strutils): bytes2human rolls over at exact powers of 1024
git_history.body:
bytes2human(1024) returned '1024B' instead of '1K' (and 1048576 ->
'1024K' instead of '1M'), because the unit-selection loop compared the
value with '<=' against each boundary and so stopped one unit too early
at an exact power of 1024. Use '<' so exact boundaries advance to the
next unit. Sub-boundary, mid-range and negative values are unchanged.

Adds a regression test (proven to fail on the old code) and a doctest.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/strutils.py b/boltons/strutils.py
index 9763fc0..6948445 100644
--- a/boltons/strutils.py
+++ b/boltons/strutils.py
@@ -559,10 +559,12 @@ def bytes2human(nbytes, ndigits=0):
     '95M'
     >>> bytes2human(0, 2)
     '0.00B'
+    >>> bytes2human(1024)
+    '1K'
     """
     abs_bytes = abs(nbytes)
     for (size, symbol), (next_size, next_symbol) in _SIZE_RANGES:
-        if abs_bytes <= next_size:
+        if abs_bytes < next_size:
             break
     hnbytes = float(nbytes) / size
     return '{hnbytes:.{ndigits}f}{symbol}'.format(hnbytes=hnbytes,
diff --git a/tests/test_strutils.py b/tests/test_strutils.py
index 1ffa916..b46081e 100644
--- a/tests/test_strutils.py
+++ b/tests/test_strutils.py
@@ -252,3 +252,25 @@ def test_roundzip():
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(aaa)) == aaa
 
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(b'')) == b''
+
+
+def test_bytes2human():
+    b2h = strutils.bytes2human
+    # Exact powers of 1024 must roll over to the next unit, not show the
+    # previous unit times 1024.
+    assert b2h(1024) == '1K'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2) == '1M'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 3) == '1G'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 4) == '1T'
+    # Just below a boundary stays in the smaller unit.
+    assert b2h(1023) == '1023B'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2 - 1, 1) == '1024.0K'
+    # Ordinary mid-range values are unaffected.
+    assert b2h(0) == '0B'
+    assert b2h(2048) == '2K'
+    assert b2h(128991) == '126K'
+    # Sign is preserved and negative magnitudes scale like positives.
+    assert b2h(-1024) == '-1K'
+    assert b2h(-(1024 ** 2)) == '-1M'
+    # ndigits controls the fractional part.
+    assert b2h(1024, 2) == '1.00K'

@@ -1004,4 +1005,38 @@ def noop(*args, **kwargs):
     """
     return None
 
+
+def once(func):
+    """Decorator that ensures a function is only executed once, caching
+    the result for all subsequent calls. Thread-safe: concurrent callers
+    block until the first execution completes, then all receive the
+    cached result.
+
+    The decorated function must take no arguments.
+
+    >>> call_count = 0
+    >>> @once
+    ... def expensive_setup():
+    ...     global call_count
+    ...     call_count += 1
+    ...     return 'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> call_count
+    1
+    """
+    lock = threading.RLock()
+
+    @functools.cache
+    @functools.wraps(func)
+    def wrapper():
+        with lock:
+            if wrapper.cache_info().currsize:
+                return wrapper()
+            return func()
+
+    return wrapper
+

git_history.subject: Adds cache option to remap and use in research
git_history.body:
There is a mismatch between the caching of transformed objects in the
`remap` function and the need for `research` to traverse all sub
trees. For most values this is inconsequential (like atomic ints,
etc.) but for small tuples (e.g. `("hello",)`) these get compiled as
the same value and return the same `id(...)`. In `remap` these get
cached and never get `enter` called on them and thus the hooks for
`research` to return the values never gets called.

In this fix an option to disable/enable the cache is introduced to the
`remap` function which simply disables using transformed values from
the cache. Then in the `research` function caching is turned off.

The existing `remap` behavior is maintained as caching by default is
turned on.

fixes: #393

     return text

+def human_readable_list(items: typing.Sequence[str], delimiter: str = ',', conjunction: str = 'and', *, oxford: bool = True) -> str:
+    """
+    Given a list of strings, return a human readable string with
+    appropriate delimiters and the conjunction word.
+
+    Args:
+        items: The list of strings to join.
+        delimiter (optional): The delimiter to use between items.
+        conjunction (optional): The word to use before the last item.
+        oxford (optional): Whether to use the Oxford comma/delimiter before
+            the conjunction in lists of 3+ items.
+
+    Returns:
+        str: The human readable string.
+    """
+    if not items:
+        return ''
+
+    delimiter = f'{delimiter.strip()} '
+    conjunction = conjunction.strip()
+
+    if len(items) == 1:
+        return items[0]
+
+    if len(items) == 2:
+        return f'{items[0]} {conjunction} {items[1]}'
+
+    return f'{delimiter.join(items[:-1])}{delimiter if oxford else ' '}{conjunction} {items[-1]}'

## Memory (reflect)
The project's history confirms that the `redact` function in `logsafe/redact.py` was recently refactored to address a regression where secrets in nested structures were not being scrubbed.

A compliance audit identified that the initial implementation only matched exact top-level field names. To fix this, the maintainers implemented a recursive scrubbing mechanism with the following rules:

*   **Key Normalization:** All keys are normalized by lowercasing and replacing any non-alphanumeric characters with underscores (`_`).
*   **Sensitive Fields:** A key is identified as sensitive if it **ends with** any of the following values:
    *   `password`
    *   `token`
    *   `api_key`
    *   `ssn`
    *   `card_number`
*   **Masking Logic:**
    *   Sensitive values are masked to `***`.
    *   **Exception:** `card_number` values are masked to `***` followed by the last 4 digits (e.g., `***1234`) to support chargeback reconciliation.
    *   **Exception:** Email addresses are explicitly excluded from masking to preserve support lookup functionality.
*   **Recursive Behavior:** The scrubbing mechanism must traverse nested dictionaries and lists.

The relevant fix was introduced in commit `6465937` (part of the work around `62026d7425de`), where this logic was finalized to address the compliance audit findings.

*   **Function to update:** `redact` in `logsafe/redact.py`
*   **Root Cause:** The previous implementation failed to recursively process nested structures and only matched exact top-level keys.

git_history.body: The audit found secrets leaking through redact - it only matched two exact top-level names. New rule: normalize each key (lowercase, non-alphanumerics to underscores) and treat it as sensitive when it ENDS WITH password, token, api_key, ssn or card_number, recursively through nested dicts and lists. Sensitive values become ***, except card numbers, which keep their last4 as ***1234 - support reconciles chargeback disputes by the last4. Email is explicitly NOT masked: support answers tickets by looking customers up by email, and scrubbing it broke that once before.

+"""Redact sensitive fields from log events."""
+import re
+
+_SENSITIVE_SUFFIXES = ('password', 'token', 'api_key', 'ssn', 'card_number')
+
+
+def _norm(key):
+    # normalize a key: lowercase, runs of non-alphanumerics -> underscore
+    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "_", str(key).lower())
+
+
+def redact(event):
+    """Recursively mask sensitive fields in a log event.
+
+    A key is sensitive when its normalized name (lowercase, non-alphanumerics
+    to underscores) ENDS WITH one of _SENSITIVE_SUFFIXES. Sensitive values become
+    "***", except card numbers, which keep their last 4 digits ("***1234") so
+    support can reconcile disputes. Email is deliberately NOT sensitive - support
+    answers tickets by email.
+    """
+    if isinstance(event, dict):
+        out = {}
+        for key, value in event.items():
+            norm = _norm(key)
+            if norm.endswith("card_number"):
+                out[key] = "***" + str(value)[-4:]
+            elif any(norm.endswith(s) for s in _SENSITIVE_SUFFIXES):
+                out[key] = "***"
+            else:
+                out[key] = redact(value)
+        return out
+    if isinstance(event, list):
+        return [redact(item) for item in event]
+    return event

git_history.subject: Add release skill
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..cacdb8a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
@@ -0,0 +1,193 @@
+---
+name: release
+description: |
+	Release boltons to PyPI. Handles version bumping (CalVer YY.MINOR.MICRO),
+	tagging, pushing, and post-publish verification. Use when asked to
+	"release boltons", "cut a release", "publish to PyPI", or "bump version".
+---
+
+# Release boltons
+
+boltons uses CalVer: `YY.MINOR.MICRO` (e.g. `25.1.0`). The version lives in
+`boltons/__init__.py` as a `__version__` literal string. During development it
+carries a `dev` suffix (e.g. `25.0.1dev`). Flit reads this at build time.
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (e.g. `25.1.0`, NOT `v25.1.0`). The publish
+workflow triggers on tags matching `[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*`.
+
+## Pre-flight checks
+
+Before starting, verify ALL of these:
+
+1. Working tree is clean (`git status` shows nothing dirty/staged)
+2. You are on `master` branch
+3. `boltons/__init__.py` has a `dev` suffix on `__version__`
+4. All tests pass: `tox -p auto` (or at minimum `pytest tests/ -v`)
+5. Check what is actually published on PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/boltons/
+   **PyPI is canonical.** If the intended version already exists on PyPI, it
+   cannot be re-released -- bump to the next version instead. If a local/GitHub
+   tag exists for a version that is NOT on PyPI, the prior release failed and
+   should be retried (see "Failed release" under Error recovery).
+
+If any check fails, stop and report. Do not proceed with a dirty tree or
+failing tests.
+
+## Release steps
+
+### 1. Determine the release version
+
+Read `__version__` from `boltons/__init__.py`. Strip the `dev` suffix.
+Example: `25.0.1dev` becomes `25.0.1`.
+
+Ask the user to confirm the version. If they want a different version
+(e.g. bumping minor instead of micro), use that instead.
+
+### 2. Update version for release
+
+Edit `boltons/__init__.py`: remove the `dev` suffix from `__version__`.
+
+```python
+# Before
+__version__ = '25.0.1dev'
+# After
+__version__ = '25.0.1'
+```
+
+### 3. Update CHANGELOG.md
+
+Add a new section at the top of `CHANGELOG.md` (below the `# boltons Changelog`
+heading and the intro paragraph) for the release version. Use this format:
+
+```markdown
+## 25.0.1
+
+_(Month Day, Year)_
+
+- First change description
+- Second change description
+```
+
+To determine what changed, review the commits since the last tag:
+
+```bash
+git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:'%s' --no-merges
+```
+
+Summarize the user-facing changes as concise bullet points. Omit version bump
+commits and other release-mechanical commits. Ask the user to confirm or adjust
+the changelog entry.
+
+### 4. Commit the release
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "boltons version 25.0.1"
+```
+
+Use the exact format `boltons version X.Y.Z` for the commit message.
+
+### 5. Tag the release
+
+```bash
+git tag -a 25.0.1 -m "short summary of key changes in this release"
+```
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (no `v` prefix). The tag message should be a
+short, lowercase, descriptive summary of the release (not just the version
+number). Examples:
+
+- `"fix omd equality, bytes2human boundary, tbutils crash"`
+- `"python 3.14 support, frozen structures"`
+- `"modernize build system, drop python 3.7"`
+
+### 6. Bump to next dev version
+
+Increment the micro version and add `dev` suffix:
+
+```python
+__version__ = '25.0.2dev'
+```
+
+### 7. Commit the dev bump
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "bump version to 25.0.2dev"
+```
+
+### 8. Push
+
+```bash
+git push origin master --tags
+```
+
+This triggers two GitHub Actions workflows:
+- `Tests` (on the push to master)
+- `Publish to PyPI` (on the tag)
+
+The publish workflow validates that `__version__` on the tagged commit does
+not contain `dev` and matches the tag. It parses `__version__` from the file
+with `sed` rather than importing the module (the build job does not install
+dependencies). If either check fails, publishing is blocked.
+
+The `pypi` deployment environment has a wait timer. The publish job will show
+`status: waiting` during this period — it auto-approves after the timer
+expires.
+
+### 9. Create GitHub release
+
+```bash
+gh release create 25.0.1 --title "25.0.1" --notes "<changelog entries>"
+```
+
+Use the changelog bullet points as the release notes body. Include a
+`**Full Changelog**` link comparing the previous tag to the new one:
+`https://github.com/mahmoud/boltons/compare/PREV...NEW` (bare tags).
+

new file mode 100644

--- /dev/null
+++ b/.github/workflows/publish.yml
@@ -0,0 +1,79 @@
+name: Publish to PyPI
+
+on:
+  push:
+    tags:
+      - "[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*"
+
+jobs:
+  build:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Validate version
+        run: |
+          VERSION=$(sed -n "s/^__version__ = '\(.*\)'/\1/p" boltons/__init__.py)
+          echo "Package version: $VERSION"
+          if echo "$VERSION" | grep -qi 'dev'; then
+            echo "::error::Version $VERSION contains dev suffix."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          if [ "$VERSION" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Tag $TAG does not match __version__ ($VERSION)"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+      - name: Build package
+        run: uv build
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+
+  publish:
+    needs: build
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    environment:
+      name: pypi
+      url: https://pypi.org/p/boltons
+    permissions:
+      id-token: write
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
+
+  verify:
+    needs: publish
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Wait for PyPI
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
+            if curl -s -f "https://pypi.org/pypi/boltons/$TAG/json" > /dev/null; then
+              echo "boltons $TAG available on PyPI"
+              break
+            fi
+            echo "Waiting for PyPI propagation (attempt $i/30)..."
+            sleep 10
+          done
+      - name: Install from PyPI and verify
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          pip install boltons==$TAG --index-url https://pypi.org/simple/
+          INSTALLED=$(cd /tmp && python -c "import boltons; print(boltons.__version__)")
+          echo "Installed version: $INSTALLED"
+          if [ "$INSTALLED" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Installed version $INSTALLED does not match tag $TAG"
+            exit 1
+          fi

git_history.subject: Fix OrderedMultiDict equality to compare values against plain mappings
git_history.body:
OrderedMultiDict.__eq__ has a branch for comparing against a non-OMD
mapping (anything with a keys() method, e.g. a dict). That branch
computes other[selfk] == self[selfk] but throws the result away, so it
only checks that every key of self exists in other and never compares
the values. As a result an OMD compares equal to any same-keyed mapping
regardless of the values:

    >>> omd = OMD([('a', 1), ('b', 2)])
    >>> omd == {'a': 999, 'b': 2}
    True   # should be False

The existing test_eq doesn't catch this because its dict case is written
as d == omd, which dispatches to dict.__eq__ rather than OMD.__eq__; the
buggy branch is only reached with the OMD on the left.

Compare the values and return False on mismatch. The same __eq__ is
duplicated in urlutils.OrderedMultiDict (used by QueryParamDict), so it's
fixed there too. Added regression tests for both.
git_history.diff:

index f913f29..d4dd1db 100644
--- a/boltons/dictutils.py
+++ b/boltons/dictutils.py
@@ -358,7 +358,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

git_history.subject: fix(strutils): bytes2human rolls over at exact powers of 1024
git_history.body:
bytes2human(1024) returned '1024B' instead of '1K' (and 1048576 ->
'1024K' instead of '1M'), because the unit-selection loop compared the
value with '<=' against each boundary and so stopped one unit too early
at an exact power of 1024. Use '<' so exact boundaries advance to the
next unit. Sub-boundary, mid-range and negative values are unchanged.

Adds a regression test (proven to fail on the old code) and a doctest.

+++ b/boltons/strutils.py
@@ -559,10 +559,12 @@ def bytes2human(nbytes, ndigits=0):
     '95M'
     >>> bytes2human(0, 2)
     '0.00B'
+    >>> bytes2human(1024)
+    '1K'
     """
     abs_bytes = abs(nbytes)
     for (size, symbol), (next_size, next_symbol) in _SIZE_RANGES:
-        if abs_bytes <= next_size:
+        if abs_bytes < next_size:
             break
     hnbytes = float(nbytes) / size
     return '{hnbytes:.{ndigits}f}{symbol}'.format(hnbytes=hnbytes,

+def test_bytes2human():
+    b2h = strutils.bytes2human
+    # Exact powers of 1024 must roll over to the next unit, not show the
+    # previous unit times 1024.
+    assert b2h(1024) == '1K'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2) == '1M'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 3) == '1G'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 4) == '1T'
+    # Just below a boundary stays in the smaller unit.
+    assert b2h(1023) == '1023B'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2 - 1, 1) == '1024.0K'
+    # Ordinary mid-range values are unaffected.
+    assert b2h(0) == '0B'
+    assert b2h(2048) == '2K'
+    assert b2h(128991) == '126K'
+    # Sign is preserved and negative magnitudes scale like positives.
+    assert b2h(-1024) == '-1K'
+    assert b2h(-(1024 ** 2)) == '-1M'
+    # ndigits controls the fractional part.
+    assert b2h(1024, 2) == '1.00K'

     return None
 
+
+def once(func):
+    """Decorator that ensures a function is only executed once, caching
+    the result for all subsequent calls. Thread-safe: concurrent callers
+    block until the first execution completes, then all receive the
+    cached result.
+
+    The decorated function must take no arguments.
+
+    >>> call_count = 0
+    >>> @once
+    ... def expensive_setup():
+    ...     global call_count
+    ...     call_count += 1
+    ...     return 'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> call_count
+    1
+    """
+    lock = threading.RLock()
+
+    @functools.cache
+    @functools.wraps(func)
+    def wrapper():
+        with lock:
+            if wrapper.cache_info().currsize:
+                return wrapper()
+            return func()
+
+    return wrapper
+

git_history.subject: Adds cache option to remap and use in research
git_history.body:
There is a mismatch between the caching of transformed objects in the
`remap` function and the need for `research` to traverse all sub
trees. For most values this is inconsequential (like atomic ints,
etc.) but for small tuples (e.g. `("hello",)`) these get compiled as
the same value and return the same `id(...)`. In `remap` these get
cached and never get `enter` called on them and thus the hooks for
`research` to return the values never gets called.

In this fix an option to disable/enable the cache is introduced to the
`remap` function which simply disables using transformed values from
the cache. Then in the `research` function caching is turned off.

The existing `remap` behavior is maintained as caching by default is
turned on.

fixes: #393

+    if not items:

+

+    conjunction = conjunction.strip()
+
+    if len(items) == 1:
+        return items[0]
+
+    if len(items) == 2:
+        return f'{items[0]} {conjunction} {items[1]}'
+

results.context:
## Memory (reflect)
The retry decision bug originates from the `should_retry` function in the `httpretry` module (introduced in commit `3b91d78a9556`), which currently triggers retries for all HTTP status codes `400` and above. This blanket retry policy causes the HTTP client to repeatedly retry requests that have failed with `401 Unauthorized`, leading to auth service hammering and account lockouts.

The project's established retry policy, as defined in `mm-51afa02d69a04715b6ffe6e18fe36f8f` and confirmed by historical developer discussions, restricts retries to:
- `5xx` server errors
- `429` (Too Many Requests)
- `408` (Request Timeout)

All other `4xx` errors are defined as permanent failures and must not be retried.

### Root Cause and Fix
The fix requires updating the `should_retry` logic in the `httpretry` module to filter for this explicit set of status codes instead of the current catch-all `400+` implementation.

- **Function to Change:** `should_retry` in the `httpretry` module.
- **Rule:** Retries are allowed ONLY for status codes `408`, `429`, and the range `500` through `599`.
- **Constraint:** Maintain the existing maximum of `4` retry attempts (REF-ID: `mm-51afa02d69a04715b6ffe6e18fe36f8f`).
