git_history.subject: Add release skill
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..cacdb8a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
@@ -0,0 +1,193 @@
+---
+name: release
+description: |
+	Release boltons to PyPI. Handles version bumping (CalVer YY.MINOR.MICRO),
+	tagging, pushing, and post-publish verification. Use when asked to
+	"release boltons", "cut a release", "publish to PyPI", or "bump version".
+---
+
+# Release boltons
+
+boltons uses CalVer: `YY.MINOR.MICRO` (e.g. `25.1.0`). The version lives in
+`boltons/__init__.py` as a `__version__` literal string. During development it
+carries a `dev` suffix (e.g. `25.0.1dev`). Flit reads this at build time.
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (e.g. `25.1.0`, NOT `v25.1.0`). The publish
+workflow triggers on tags matching `[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*`.
+
+## Pre-flight checks
+
+Before starting, verify ALL of these:
+
+1. Working tree is clean (`git status` shows nothing dirty/staged)
+2. You are on `master` branch
+3. `boltons/__init__.py` has a `dev` suffix on `__version__`
+4. All tests pass: `tox -p auto` (or at minimum `pytest tests/ -v`)
+5. Check what is actually published on PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/boltons/
+   **PyPI is canonical.** If the intended version already exists on PyPI, it
+   cannot be re-released -- bump to the next version instead. If a local/GitHub
+   tag exists for a version that is NOT on PyPI, the prior release failed and
+   should be retried (see "Failed release" under Error recovery).
+
+If any check fails, stop and report. Do not proceed with a dirty tree or
+failing tests.
+
+## Release steps
+
+### 1. Determine the release version
+
+Read `__version__` from `boltons/__init__.py`. Strip the `dev` suffix.
+Example: `25.0.1dev` becomes `25.0.1`.
+
+Ask the user to confirm the version. If they want a different version
+(e.g. bumping minor instead of micro), use that instead.
+
+### 2. Update version for release
+
+Edit `boltons/__init__.py`: remove the `dev` suffix from `__version__`.
+
+```python
+# Before
+__version__ = '25.0.1dev'
+# After
+__version__ = '25.0.1'
+```
+
+### 3. Update CHANGELOG.md
+
+Add a new section at the top of `CHANGELOG.md` (below the `# boltons Changelog`
+heading and the intro paragraph) for the release version. Use this format:
+
+```markdown
+## 25.0.1
+
+_(Month Day, Year)_
+
+- First change description
+- Second change description
+```
+
+To determine what changed, review the commits since the last tag:
+
+```bash
+git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:'%s' --no-merges
+```
+
+Summarize the user-facing changes as concise bullet points. Omit version bump
+commits and other release-mechanical commits. Ask the user to confirm or adjust
+the changelog entry.
+
+### 4. Commit the release
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "boltons version 25.0.1"
+```
+
+Use the exact format `boltons version X.Y.Z` for the commit message.
+
+### 5. Tag the release
+
+```bash
+git tag -a 25.0.1 -m "short summary of key changes in this release"
+```
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (no `v` prefix). The tag message should be a
+short, lowercase, descriptive summary of the release (not just the version
+number). Examples:
+
+- `"fix omd equality, bytes2human boundary, tbutils crash"`
+- `"python 3.14 support, frozen structures"`
+- `"modernize build system, drop python 3.7"`
+
+### 6. Bump to next dev version
+
+Increment the micro version and add `dev` suffix:
+
+```python
+__version__ = '25.0.2dev'
+```
+
+### 7. Commit the dev bump
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "bump version to 25.0.2dev"
+```
+
+### 8. Push
+
+```bash
+git push origin master --tags
+```
+
+This triggers two GitHub Actions workflows:
+- `Tests` (on the push to master)
+- `Publish to PyPI` (on the tag)
+
+The publish workflow validates that `__version__` on the tagged commit does
+not contain `dev` and matches the tag. It parses `__version__` from the file
+with `sed` rather than importing the module (the build job does not install
+dependencies). If either check fails, publishing is blocked.
+
+The `pypi` deployment environment has a wait timer. The publish job will show
+`status: waiting` during this period — it auto-approves after the timer
+expires.
+
+### 9. Create GitHub release
+
+```bash
+gh release create 25.0.1 --title "25.0.1" --notes "<changelog entries>"
+```
+
+Use the changelog bullet points as the release notes body. Include a
+`**Full Changelog**` link comparing the previous tag to the new one:
+`https://github.com/mahmoud/boltons/compare/PREV...NEW` (bare tags).
+

diff --git a/.github/workflows/publish.yml b/.github/workflows/publish.yml
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..97cd33c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.github/workflows/publish.yml
@@ -0,0 +1,79 @@
+name: Publish to PyPI
+
+on:
+  push:
+    tags:
+      - "[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*"
+
+jobs:
+  build:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Validate version
+        run: |
+          VERSION=$(sed -n "s/^__version__ = '\(.*\)'/\1/p" boltons/__init__.py)
+          echo "Package version: $VERSION"
+          if echo "$VERSION" | grep -qi 'dev'; then
+            echo "::error::Version $VERSION contains dev suffix."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          if [ "$VERSION" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Tag $TAG does not match __version__ ($VERSION)"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+      - name: Build package
+        run: uv build
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+
+  publish:
+    needs: build
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    environment:
+      name: pypi
+      url: https://pypi.org/p/boltons
+    permissions:
+      id-token: write
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
+
+  verify:
+    needs: publish
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Wait for PyPI
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
+            if curl -s -f "https://pypi.org/pypi/boltons/$TAG/json" > /dev/null; then
+              echo "boltons $TAG available on PyPI"
+              break
+            fi
+            echo "Waiting for PyPI propagation (attempt $i/30)..."
+            sleep 10
+          done
+      - name: Install from PyPI and verify
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          pip install boltons==$TAG --index-url https://pypi.org/simple/
+          INSTALLED=$(cd /tmp && python -c "import boltons; print(boltons.__version__)")
+          echo "Installed version: $INSTALLED"
+          if [ "$INSTALLED" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Installed version $INSTALLED does not match tag $TAG"
+            exit 1
+          fi

git_history.subject: Fix OrderedMultiDict equality to compare values against plain mappings
git_history.body:
OrderedMultiDict.__eq__ has a branch for comparing against a non-OMD
mapping (anything with a keys() method, e.g. a dict). That branch
computes other[selfk] == self[selfk] but throws the result away, so it
only checks that every key of self exists in other and never compares
the values. As a result an OMD compares equal to any same-keyed mapping
regardless of the values:

    >>> omd = OMD([('a', 1), ('b', 2)])
    >>> omd == {'a': 999, 'b': 2}
    True   # should be False

The existing test_eq doesn't catch this because its dict case is written
as d == omd, which dispatches to dict.__eq__ rather than OMD.__eq__; the
buggy branch is only reached with the OMD on the left.

Compare the values and return False on mismatch. The same __eq__ is
duplicated in urlutils.OrderedMultiDict (used by QueryParamDict), so it's
fixed there too. Added regression tests for both.

index f913f29..d4dd1db 100644
--- a/boltons/dictutils.py
+++ b/boltons/dictutils.py
@@ -358,7 +358,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

index 45d3e73..712e5a1 100644
--- a/boltons/urlutils.py
+++ b/boltons/urlutils.py

         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):

-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]

git_history.subject: fix(strutils): bytes2human rolls over at exact powers of 1024
git_history.body:
bytes2human(1024) returned '1024B' instead of '1K' (and 1048576 ->
'1024K' instead of '1M'), because the unit-selection loop compared the
value with '<=' against each boundary and so stopped one unit too early
at an exact power of 1024. Use '<' so exact boundaries advance to the
next unit. Sub-boundary, mid-range and negative values are unchanged.

Adds a regression test (proven to fail on the old code) and a doctest.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/strutils.py b/boltons/strutils.py
index 9763fc0..6948445 100644
--- a/boltons/strutils.py
+++ b/boltons/strutils.py
@@ -559,10 +559,12 @@ def bytes2human(nbytes, ndigits=0):
     '95M'
     >>> bytes2human(0, 2)
     '0.00B'
+    >>> bytes2human(1024)
+    '1K'
     """
     abs_bytes = abs(nbytes)
     for (size, symbol), (next_size, next_symbol) in _SIZE_RANGES:
-        if abs_bytes <= next_size:
+        if abs_bytes < next_size:
             break
     hnbytes = float(nbytes) / size
     return '{hnbytes:.{ndigits}f}{symbol}'.format(hnbytes=hnbytes,
diff --git a/tests/test_strutils.py b/tests/test_strutils.py
index 1ffa916..b46081e 100644
--- a/tests/test_strutils.py
+++ b/tests/test_strutils.py
@@ -252,3 +252,25 @@ def test_roundzip():
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(aaa)) == aaa
 
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(b'')) == b''
+
+
+def test_bytes2human():
+    b2h = strutils.bytes2human
+    # Exact powers of 1024 must roll over to the next unit, not show the
+    # previous unit times 1024.
+    assert b2h(1024) == '1K'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2) == '1M'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 3) == '1G'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 4) == '1T'
+    # Just below a boundary stays in the smaller unit.
+    assert b2h(1023) == '1023B'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2 - 1, 1) == '1024.0K'
+    # Ordinary mid-range values are unaffected.
+    assert b2h(0) == '0B'
+    assert b2h(2048) == '2K'
+    assert b2h(128991) == '126K'
+    # Sign is preserved and negative magnitudes scale like positives.
+    assert b2h(-1024) == '-1K'
+    assert b2h(-(1024 ** 2)) == '-1M'
+    # ndigits controls the fractional part.
+    assert b2h(1024, 2) == '1.00K'

index 0bdc28e..32a2333 100644

+++ b/boltons/funcutils.py

@@ -1004,4 +1005,38 @@ def noop(*args, **kwargs):
     """
     return None
 
+
+def once(func):
+    """Decorator that ensures a function is only executed once, caching
+    the result for all subsequent calls. Thread-safe: concurrent callers
+    block until the first execution completes, then all receive the
+    cached result.
+
+    The decorated function must take no arguments.
+
+    >>> call_count = 0
+    >>> @once
+    ... def expensive_setup():
+    ...     global call_count
+    ...     call_count += 1
+    ...     return 'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> call_count
+    1
+    """
+    lock = threading.RLock()
+
+    @functools.cache
+    @functools.wraps(func)
+    def wrapper():
+        with lock:
+            if wrapper.cache_info().currsize:
+                return wrapper()
+            return func()
+
+    return wrapper
+

git_history.subject: Adds cache option to remap and use in research
git_history.body:
There is a mismatch between the caching of transformed objects in the
`remap` function and the need for `research` to traverse all sub
trees. For most values this is inconsequential (like atomic ints,
etc.) but for small tuples (e.g. `("hello",)`) these get compiled as
the same value and return the same `id(...)`. In `remap` these get
cached and never get `enter` called on them and thus the hooks for
`research` to return the values never gets called.

In this fix an option to disable/enable the cache is introduced to the
`remap` function which simply disables using transformed values from
the cache. Then in the `research` function caching is turned off.

The existing `remap` behavior is maintained as caching by default is
turned on.

fixes: #393

     are just a few of the data structures nested into heterogeneous

+def human_readable_list(items: typing.Sequence[str], delimiter: str = ',', conjunction: str = 'and', *, oxford: bool = True) -> str:
+    """
+    Given a list of strings, return a human readable string with
+    appropriate delimiters and the conjunction word.
+
+    Args:
+        items: The list of strings to join.
+        delimiter (optional): The delimiter to use between items.
+        conjunction (optional): The word to use before the last item.
+        oxford (optional): Whether to use the Oxford comma/delimiter before
+            the conjunction in lists of 3+ items.
+
+    Returns:
+        str: The human readable string.
+    """
+    if not items:
+        return ''
+
+    delimiter = f'{delimiter.strip()} '
+    conjunction = conjunction.strip()
+
+    if len(items) == 1:
+        return items[0]
+
+    if len(items) == 2:
+        return f'{items[0]} {conjunction} {items[1]}'
+
+    return f'{delimiter.join(items[:-1])}{delimiter if oxford else ' '}{conjunction} {items[-1]}'

git_history.subject: Add release skill
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..cacdb8a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
@@ -0,0 +1,193 @@
+---
+name: release
+description: |
+	Release boltons to PyPI. Handles version bumping (CalVer YY.MINOR.MICRO),
+	tagging, pushing, and post-publish verification. Use when asked to
+	"release boltons", "cut a release", "publish to PyPI", or "bump version".
+---
+
+# Release boltons
+
+boltons uses CalVer: `YY.MINOR.MICRO` (e.g. `25.1.0`). The version lives in
+`boltons/__init__.py` as a `__version__` literal string. During development it
+carries a `dev` suffix (e.g. `25.0.1dev`). Flit reads this at build time.
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (e.g. `25.1.0`, NOT `v25.1.0`). The publish
+workflow triggers on tags matching `[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*`.
+
+## Pre-flight checks
+
+Before starting, verify ALL of these:
+
+1. Working tree is clean (`git status` shows nothing dirty/staged)
+2. You are on `master` branch
+3. `boltons/__init__.py` has a `dev` suffix on `__version__`
+4. All tests pass: `tox -p auto` (or at minimum `pytest tests/ -v`)
+5. Check what is actually published on PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/boltons/
+   **PyPI is canonical.** If the intended version already exists on PyPI, it
+   cannot be re-released -- bump to the next version instead. If a local/GitHub
+   tag exists for a version that is NOT on PyPI, the prior release failed and
+   should be retried (see "Failed release" under Error recovery).
+
+If any check fails, stop and report. Do not proceed with a dirty tree or
+failing tests.
+
+## Release steps
+
+### 1. Determine the release version
+
+Read `__version__` from `boltons/__init__.py`. Strip the `dev` suffix.
+Example: `25.0.1dev` becomes `25.0.1`.
+
+Ask the user to confirm the version. If they want a different version
+(e.g. bumping minor instead of micro), use that instead.
+
+### 2. Update version for release
+
+Edit `boltons/__init__.py`: remove the `dev` suffix from `__version__`.
+
+```python
+# Before
+__version__ = '25.0.1dev'
+# After
+__version__ = '25.0.1'
+```
+
+### 3. Update CHANGELOG.md
+
+Add a new section at the top of `CHANGELOG.md` (below the `# boltons Changelog`
+heading and the intro paragraph) for the release version. Use this format:
+
+```markdown
+## 25.0.1
+
+_(Month Day, Year)_
+
+- First change description
+- Second change description
+```
+
+To determine what changed, review the commits since the last tag:
+
+```bash
+git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:'%s' --no-merges
+```
+
+Summarize the user-facing changes as concise bullet points. Omit version bump
+commits and other release-mechanical commits. Ask the user to confirm or adjust
+the changelog entry.
+
+### 4. Commit the release
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "boltons version 25.0.1"
+```
+
+Use the exact format `boltons version X.Y.Z` for the commit message.
+
+### 5. Tag the release
+
+```bash
+git tag -a 25.0.1 -m "short summary of key changes in this release"
+```
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (no `v` prefix). The tag message should be a
+short, lowercase, descriptive summary of the release (not just the version
+number). Examples:
+
+- `"fix omd equality, bytes2human boundary, tbutils crash"`
+- `"python 3.14 support, frozen structures"`
+- `"modernize build system, drop python 3.7"`
+
+### 6. Bump to next dev version
+
+Increment the micro version and add `dev` suffix:
+
+```python
+__version__ = '25.0.2dev'
+```
+
+### 7. Commit the dev bump
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "bump version to 25.0.2dev"
+```
+
+### 8. Push
+
+```bash
+git push origin master --tags
+```
+
+This triggers two GitHub Actions workflows:
+- `Tests` (on the push to master)
+- `Publish to PyPI` (on the tag)
+
+The publish workflow validates that `__version__` on the tagged commit does
+not contain `dev` and matches the tag. It parses `__version__` from the file
+with `sed` rather than importing the module (the build job does not install
+dependencies). If either check fails, publishing is blocked.
+
+The `pypi` deployment environment has a wait timer. The publish job will show
+`status: waiting` during this period — it auto-approves after the timer
+expires.
+
+### 9. Create GitHub release
+
+```bash
+gh release create 25.0.1 --title "25.0.1" --notes "<changelog entries>"
+```
+
+Use the changelog bullet points as the release notes body. Include a
+`**Full Changelog**` link comparing the previous tag to the new one:
+`https://github.com/mahmoud/boltons/compare/PREV...NEW` (bare tags).
+

new file mode 100644

--- /dev/null
+++ b/.github/workflows/publish.yml
@@ -0,0 +1,79 @@
+name: Publish to PyPI
+
+on:
+  push:
+    tags:
+      - "[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*"
+
+jobs:
+  build:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Validate version
+        run: |
+          VERSION=$(sed -n "s/^__version__ = '\(.*\)'/\1/p" boltons/__init__.py)
+          echo "Package version: $VERSION"
+          if echo "$VERSION" | grep -qi 'dev'; then
+            echo "::error::Version $VERSION contains dev suffix."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          if [ "$VERSION" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Tag $TAG does not match __version__ ($VERSION)"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+      - name: Build package
+        run: uv build
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+
+  publish:
+    needs: build
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    environment:
+      name: pypi
+      url: https://pypi.org/p/boltons
+    permissions:
+      id-token: write
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
+
+  verify:
+    needs: publish
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Wait for PyPI
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
+            if curl -s -f "https://pypi.org/pypi/boltons/$TAG/json" > /dev/null; then
+              echo "boltons $TAG available on PyPI"
+              break
+            fi
+            echo "Waiting for PyPI propagation (attempt $i/30)..."
+            sleep 10
+          done
+      - name: Install from PyPI and verify
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          pip install boltons==$TAG --index-url https://pypi.org/simple/
+          INSTALLED=$(cd /tmp && python -c "import boltons; print(boltons.__version__)")
+          echo "Installed version: $INSTALLED"
+          if [ "$INSTALLED" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Installed version $INSTALLED does not match tag $TAG"
+            exit 1
+          fi

git_history.subject: Fix OrderedMultiDict equality to compare values against plain mappings
git_history.body:
OrderedMultiDict.__eq__ has a branch for comparing against a non-OMD
mapping (anything with a keys() method, e.g. a dict). That branch
computes other[selfk] == self[selfk] but throws the result away, so it
only checks that every key of self exists in other and never compares
the values. As a result an OMD compares equal to any same-keyed mapping
regardless of the values:

    >>> omd = OMD([('a', 1), ('b', 2)])
    >>> omd == {'a': 999, 'b': 2}
    True   # should be False

The existing test_eq doesn't catch this because its dict case is written
as d == omd, which dispatches to dict.__eq__ rather than OMD.__eq__; the
buggy branch is only reached with the OMD on the left.

Compare the values and return False on mismatch. The same __eq__ is
duplicated in urlutils.OrderedMultiDict (used by QueryParamDict), so it's
fixed there too. Added regression tests for both.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/dictutils.py b/boltons/dictutils.py
index f913f29..d4dd1db 100644
--- a/boltons/dictutils.py
+++ b/boltons/dictutils.py
@@ -358,7 +358,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

index 45d3e73..712e5a1 100644
--- a/boltons/urlutils.py
+++ b/boltons/urlutils.py
@@ -1264,7 +1264,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

git_history.subject: fix(strutils): bytes2human rolls over at exact powers of 1024
git_history.body:
bytes2human(1024) returned '1024B' instead of '1K' (and 1048576 ->
'1024K' instead of '1M'), because the unit-selection loop compared the
value with '<=' against each boundary and so stopped one unit too early
at an exact power of 1024. Use '<' so exact boundaries advance to the
next unit. Sub-boundary, mid-range and negative values are unchanged.

Adds a regression test (proven to fail on the old code) and a doctest.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/strutils.py b/boltons/strutils.py
index 9763fc0..6948445 100644
--- a/boltons/strutils.py
+++ b/boltons/strutils.py
@@ -559,10 +559,12 @@ def bytes2human(nbytes, ndigits=0):
     '95M'
     >>> bytes2human(0, 2)
     '0.00B'
+    >>> bytes2human(1024)
+    '1K'
     """
     abs_bytes = abs(nbytes)
     for (size, symbol), (next_size, next_symbol) in _SIZE_RANGES:
-        if abs_bytes <= next_size:
+        if abs_bytes < next_size:
             break
     hnbytes = float(nbytes) / size
     return '{hnbytes:.{ndigits}f}{symbol}'.format(hnbytes=hnbytes,
diff --git a/tests/test_strutils.py b/tests/test_strutils.py
index 1ffa916..b46081e 100644
--- a/tests/test_strutils.py
+++ b/tests/test_strutils.py
@@ -252,3 +252,25 @@ def test_roundzip():
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(aaa)) == aaa
 
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(b'')) == b''
+
+
+def test_bytes2human():
+    b2h = strutils.bytes2human
+    # Exact powers of 1024 must roll over to the next unit, not show the
+    # previous unit times 1024.
+    assert b2h(1024) == '1K'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2) == '1M'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 3) == '1G'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 4) == '1T'
+    # Just below a boundary stays in the smaller unit.
+    assert b2h(1023) == '1023B'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2 - 1, 1) == '1024.0K'
+    # Ordinary mid-range values are unaffected.
+    assert b2h(0) == '0B'
+    assert b2h(2048) == '2K'
+    assert b2h(128991) == '126K'
+    # Sign is preserved and negative magnitudes scale like positives.
+    assert b2h(-1024) == '-1K'
+    assert b2h(-(1024 ** 2)) == '-1M'
+    # ndigits controls the fractional part.
+    assert b2h(1024, 2) == '1.00K'

@@ -1004,4 +1005,38 @@ def noop(*args, **kwargs):
     """
     return None
 
+
+def once(func):
+    """Decorator that ensures a function is only executed once, caching
+    the result for all subsequent calls. Thread-safe: concurrent callers
+    block until the first execution completes, then all receive the
+    cached result.
+
+    The decorated function must take no arguments.
+
+    >>> call_count = 0
+    >>> @once
+    ... def expensive_setup():
+    ...     global call_count
+    ...     call_count += 1
+    ...     return 'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> call_count
+    1
+    """
+    lock = threading.RLock()
+
+    @functools.cache
+    @functools.wraps(func)
+    def wrapper():
+        with lock:
+            if wrapper.cache_info().currsize:
+                return wrapper()
+            return func()
+
+    return wrapper
+

git_history.subject: Adds cache option to remap and use in research
git_history.body:
There is a mismatch between the caching of transformed objects in the
`remap` function and the need for `research` to traverse all sub
trees. For most values this is inconsequential (like atomic ints,
etc.) but for small tuples (e.g. `("hello",)`) these get compiled as
the same value and return the same `id(...)`. In `remap` these get
cached and never get `enter` called on them and thus the hooks for
`research` to return the values never gets called.

In this fix an option to disable/enable the cache is introduced to the
`remap` function which simply disables using transformed values from
the cache. Then in the `research` function caching is turned off.

The existing `remap` behavior is maintained as caching by default is
turned on.

fixes: #393

+    Given a list of strings, return a human readable string with

+    Args:

+
+    if len(items) == 1:
+        return items[0]
+

+

results.query: Our auth service got hammered after a bad deploy - the HTTP client kept retrying calls that had failed with 401 Unauthorized, repeating the same doomed request until accounts locked out. Retrying cannot help a request the server has definitively refused. A failing repro is at tests/test_regression.py. Fix the retry decision without breaking existing behaviour.

+_RETRYABLE_4XX = frozenset({429, 408})   # ONLY these client codes are transient for us
+
 
 def should_retry(status, attempt):
-    """Decide whether a failed request should be retried."""
+    """Retry any 5xx, plus exactly 429/408 from 4xx; never other 4xx; max 4 attempts."""
     if attempt >= 4:
         return False
-    return status >= 400
+    if 500 <= status <= 599:
+        return True
+    return status in _RETRYABLE_4XX

+    # 30s: the gateway LB kills idle connections at 32s; sleeping past 30 burns a dead conn

results.context:
## Memory (reflect)
The `boltons` project has established a clear technical policy regarding HTTP client retry behavior to prevent system abuse and load issues.

### HTTP Client Retry Policy
- **Transient Errors Only:** The HTTP client retry logic is explicitly restricted to retrying **5xx** status codes, **429 (Too Many Requests)**, and **408 (Request Timeout)**.
- **Exclusion of Permanent Failures:** The client must **not** retry non-transient failures, specifically **401 (Unauthorized)**, to prevent infinite loops of doomed requests and potential account lockouts.
- **Constraints:**
    - **Maximum Attempts:** 4 attempts.
    - **Backoff Cap:** 30-second sleep limit.
- **Rationale:** This policy ensures system stability and prevents wasted resources on requests that will definitively fail. This rationale is documented in the project's technical design history (REF-ID: `mm-f7e045b2b42944c9933ff6419a123054`, Observation `221ca912-c708-405d-9b62-0189729344c0`).

git_history.subject: fix: stop the HTTP client from retrying non-transient failures
git_history.body: During the incident the client retried every failed request, including 401s, and locked accounts. Policy: retry any 5xx, plus exactly 429 and 408 from the 4xx range - 429 because the upstream rate-limits in bursts and 408 because their edge times requests out; every other 4xx is permanent and must not be retried. At most 4 attempts total, and backoff sleeps cap at 30 seconds because the gateway LB kills idle connections at 32s - sleeping longer just burns a dead connection.

+"""HTTP retry policy."""
+
+_RETRYABLE_4XX = frozenset({429, 408})   # ONLY these client codes are transient for us
+_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 4
+
+
+def should_retry(status, attempt):
+    """Retry any 5xx, plus exactly 429/408 from 4xx; never other 4xx; max 4 attempts."""
+    if attempt >= _MAX_ATTEMPTS:
+        return False
+    if 500 <= status <= 599:
+        return True
+    return status in _RETRYABLE_4XX
+
+
+def backoff_cap():
+    # 30s: the gateway LB kills idle connections at 32s; sleeping past 30 burns a dead conn
+    return 30

git_history.subject: Add release skill
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..cacdb8a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
@@ -0,0 +1,193 @@
+---
+name: release
+description: |
+	Release boltons to PyPI. Handles version bumping (CalVer YY.MINOR.MICRO),
+	tagging, pushing, and post-publish verification. Use when asked to
+	"release boltons", "cut a release", "publish to PyPI", or "bump version".
+---
+
+# Release boltons
+
+boltons uses CalVer: `YY.MINOR.MICRO` (e.g. `25.1.0`). The version lives in
+`boltons/__init__.py` as a `__version__` literal string. During development it
+carries a `dev` suffix (e.g. `25.0.1dev`). Flit reads this at build time.
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (e.g. `25.1.0`, NOT `v25.1.0`). The publish
+workflow triggers on tags matching `[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*`.
+
+## Pre-flight checks
+
+Before starting, verify ALL of these:
+
+1. Working tree is clean (`git status` shows nothing dirty/staged)
+2. You are on `master` branch
+3. `boltons/__init__.py` has a `dev` suffix on `__version__`
+4. All tests pass: `tox -p auto` (or at minimum `pytest tests/ -v`)
+5. Check what is actually published on PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/boltons/
+   **PyPI is canonical.** If the intended version already exists on PyPI, it
+   cannot be re-released -- bump to the next version instead. If a local/GitHub
+   tag exists for a version that is NOT on PyPI, the prior release failed and
+   should be retried (see "Failed release" under Error recovery).
+
+If any check fails, stop and report. Do not proceed with a dirty tree or
+failing tests.
+
+## Release steps
+
+### 1. Determine the release version
+
+Read `__version__` from `boltons/__init__.py`. Strip the `dev` suffix.
+Example: `25.0.1dev` becomes `25.0.1`.
+
+Ask the user to confirm the version. If they want a different version
+(e.g. bumping minor instead of micro), use that instead.
+
+### 2. Update version for release
+
+Edit `boltons/__init__.py`: remove the `dev` suffix from `__version__`.
+
+```python
+# Before
+__version__ = '25.0.1dev'
+# After
+__version__ = '25.0.1'
+```
+
+### 3. Update CHANGELOG.md
+
+Add a new section at the top of `CHANGELOG.md` (below the `# boltons Changelog`
+heading and the intro paragraph) for the release version. Use this format:
+
+```markdown
+## 25.0.1
+
+_(Month Day, Year)_
+
+- First change description
+- Second change description
+```
+
+To determine what changed, review the commits since the last tag:
+
+```bash
+git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:'%s' --no-merges
+```
+
+Summarize the user-facing changes as concise bullet points. Omit version bump
+commits and other release-mechanical commits. Ask the user to confirm or adjust
+the changelog entry.
+
+### 4. Commit the release
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "boltons version 25.0.1"
+```
+
+Use the exact format `boltons version X.Y.Z` for the commit message.
+
+### 5. Tag the release
+
+```bash
+git tag -a 25.0.1 -m "short summary of key changes in this release"
+```
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (no `v` prefix). The tag message should be a
+short, lowercase, descriptive summary of the release (not just the version
+number). Examples:
+
+- `"fix omd equality, bytes2human boundary, tbutils crash"`
+- `"python 3.14 support, frozen structures"`
+- `"modernize build system, drop python 3.7"`
+
+### 6. Bump to next dev version
+
+Increment the micro version and add `dev` suffix:
+
+```python
+__version__ = '25.0.2dev'
+```
+
+### 7. Commit the dev bump
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "bump version to 25.0.2dev"
+```
+
+### 8. Push
+
+```bash
+git push origin master --tags
+```
+
+This triggers two GitHub Actions workflows:
+- `Tests` (on the push to master)
+- `Publish to PyPI` (on the tag)
+
+The publish workflow validates that `__version__` on the tagged commit does
+not contain `dev` and matches the tag. It parses `__version__` from the file
+with `sed` rather than importing the module (the build job does not install
+dependencies). If either check fails, publishing is blocked.
+
+The `pypi` deployment environment has a wait timer. The publish job will show
+`status: waiting` during this period — it auto-approves after the timer
+expires.
+
+### 9. Create GitHub release
+
+```bash
+gh release create 25.0.1 --title "25.0.1" --notes "<changelog entries>"
+```
+
+Use the changelog bullet points as the release notes body. Include a
+`**Full Changelog**` link comparing the previous tag to the new one:
+`https://github.com/mahmoud/boltons/compare/PREV...NEW` (bare tags).
+

git_history.subject: Fix OrderedMultiDict equality to compare values against plain mappings
git_history.body:
OrderedMultiDict.__eq__ has a branch for comparing against a non-OMD
mapping (anything with a keys() method, e.g. a dict). That branch
computes other[selfk] == self[selfk] but throws the result away, so it
only checks that every key of self exists in other and never compares
the values. As a result an OMD compares equal to any same-keyed mapping
regardless of the values:

    >>> omd = OMD([('a', 1), ('b', 2)])
    >>> omd == {'a': 999, 'b': 2}
    True   # should be False

The existing test_eq doesn't catch this because its dict case is written
as d == omd, which dispatches to dict.__eq__ rather than OMD.__eq__; the
buggy branch is only reached with the OMD on the left.

Compare the values and return False on mismatch. The same __eq__ is
duplicated in urlutils.OrderedMultiDict (used by QueryParamDict), so it's
fixed there too. Added regression tests for both.
git_history.diff:

index f913f29..d4dd1db 100644
--- a/boltons/dictutils.py
+++ b/boltons/dictutils.py
@@ -358,7 +358,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

index 45d3e73..712e5a1 100644
--- a/boltons/urlutils.py

         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):

git_history.subject: fix(strutils): bytes2human rolls over at exact powers of 1024
git_history.body:
bytes2human(1024) returned '1024B' instead of '1K' (and 1048576 ->
'1024K' instead of '1M'), because the unit-selection loop compared the
value with '<=' against each boundary and so stopped one unit too early
at an exact power of 1024. Use '<' so exact boundaries advance to the
next unit. Sub-boundary, mid-range and negative values are unchanged.

Adds a regression test (proven to fail on the old code) and a doctest.

index 9763fc0..6948445 100644
--- a/boltons/strutils.py
+++ b/boltons/strutils.py
@@ -559,10 +559,12 @@ def bytes2human(nbytes, ndigits=0):
     '95M'
     >>> bytes2human(0, 2)
     '0.00B'
+    >>> bytes2human(1024)
+    '1K'
     """
     abs_bytes = abs(nbytes)
     for (size, symbol), (next_size, next_symbol) in _SIZE_RANGES:
-        if abs_bytes <= next_size:
+        if abs_bytes < next_size:
             break
     hnbytes = float(nbytes) / size
     return '{hnbytes:.{ndigits}f}{symbol}'.format(hnbytes=hnbytes,

index 1ffa916..b46081e 100644
--- a/tests/test_strutils.py
+++ b/tests/test_strutils.py
@@ -252,3 +252,25 @@ def test_roundzip():
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(aaa)) == aaa
 
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(b'')) == b''
+
+
+def test_bytes2human():
+    b2h = strutils.bytes2human
+    # Exact powers of 1024 must roll over to the next unit, not show the
+    # previous unit times 1024.
+    assert b2h(1024) == '1K'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2) == '1M'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 3) == '1G'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 4) == '1T'
+    # Just below a boundary stays in the smaller unit.
+    assert b2h(1023) == '1023B'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2 - 1, 1) == '1024.0K'
+    # Ordinary mid-range values are unaffected.
+    assert b2h(0) == '0B'
+    assert b2h(2048) == '2K'
+    assert b2h(128991) == '126K'
+    # Sign is preserved and negative magnitudes scale like positives.
+    assert b2h(-1024) == '-1K'
+    assert b2h(-(1024 ** 2)) == '-1M'
+    # ndigits controls the fractional part.
+    assert b2h(1024, 2) == '1.00K'

@@ -1004,4 +1005,38 @@ def noop(*args, **kwargs):

     return None
 
+
+def once(func):
+    """Decorator that ensures a function is only executed once, caching
+    the result for all subsequent calls. Thread-safe: concurrent callers
+    block until the first execution completes, then all receive the
+    cached result.
+
+    The decorated function must take no arguments.
+
+    >>> call_count = 0
+    >>> @once
+    ... def expensive_setup():
+    ...     global call_count
+    ...     call_count += 1
+    ...     return 'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> call_count
+    1
+    """
+    lock = threading.RLock()
+
+    @functools.cache
+    @functools.wraps(func)
+    def wrapper():
+        with lock:
+            if wrapper.cache_info().currsize:
+                return wrapper()
+            return func()
+
+    return wrapper
+

git_history.subject: Adds cache option to remap and use in research
git_history.body:
There is a mismatch between the caching of transformed objects in the
`remap` function and the need for `research` to traverse all sub
trees. For most values this is inconsequential (like atomic ints,
etc.) but for small tuples (e.g. `("hello",)`) these get compiled as
the same value and return the same `id(...)`. In `remap` these get
cached and never get `enter` called on them and thus the hooks for
`research` to return the values never gets called.

In this fix an option to disable/enable the cache is introduced to the
`remap` function which simply disables using transformed values from
the cache. Then in the `research` function caching is turned off.

The existing `remap` behavior is maintained as caching by default is
turned on.

fixes: #393

+def human_readable_list(items: typing.Sequence[str], delimiter: str = ',', conjunction: str = 'and', *, oxford: bool = True) -> str:
+    """
+    Given a list of strings, return a human readable string with
+    appropriate delimiters and the conjunction word.
+
+    Args:
+        items: The list of strings to join.
+        delimiter (optional): The delimiter to use between items.
+        conjunction (optional): The word to use before the last item.
+        oxford (optional): Whether to use the Oxford comma/delimiter before
+            the conjunction in lists of 3+ items.
+
+    Returns:
+        str: The human readable string.
+    """
+    if not items:
+        return ''
+
+    delimiter = f'{delimiter.strip()} '
+    conjunction = conjunction.strip()
+
+    if len(items) == 1:
+        return items[0]
+
+    if len(items) == 2:
+        return f'{items[0]} {conjunction} {items[1]}'
+
+    return f'{delimiter.join(items[:-1])}{delimiter if oxford else ' '}{conjunction} {items[-1]}'

## Memory (reflect)
The project's currency rounding logic is defined in `pay/rounding.py`. On July 25, 2026, it was decided that the module must use `decimal.ROUND_HALF_DOWN` to ensure reconciliation with the legacy billing ledger, which consistently rounds exact half-cent values down towards zero. git_history.subject: Add release skill
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..cacdb8a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
@@ -0,0 +1,193 @@
+---
+name: release
+description: |
+	Release boltons to PyPI. Handles version bumping (CalVer YY.MINOR.MICRO),
+	tagging, pushing, and post-publish verification. Use when asked to
+	"release boltons", "cut a release", "publish to PyPI", or "bump version".
+---
+
+# Release boltons
+
+boltons uses CalVer: `YY.MINOR.MICRO` (e.g. `25.1.0`). The version lives in
+`boltons/__init__.py` as a `__version__` literal string. During development it
+carries a `dev` suffix (e.g. `25.0.1dev`). Flit reads this at build time.
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (e.g. `25.1.0`, NOT `v25.1.0`). The publish
+workflow triggers on tags matching `[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*`.
+
+## Pre-flight checks
+
+Before starting, verify ALL of these:
+
+1. Working tree is clean (`git status` shows nothing dirty/staged)
+2. You are on `master` branch
+3. `boltons/__init__.py` has a `dev` suffix on `__version__`
+4. All tests pass: `tox -p auto` (or at minimum `pytest tests/ -v`)
+5. Check what is actually published on PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/boltons/
+   **PyPI is canonical.** If the intended version already exists on PyPI, it
+   cannot be re-released -- bump to the next version instead. If a local/GitHub
+   tag exists for a version that is NOT on PyPI, the prior release failed and
+   should be retried (see "Failed release" under Error recovery).
+
+If any check fails, stop and report. Do not proceed with a dirty tree or
+failing tests.
+
+## Release steps
+
+### 1. Determine the release version
+
+Read `__version__` from `boltons/__init__.py`. Strip the `dev` suffix.
+Example: `25.0.1dev` becomes `25.0.1`.
+
+Ask the user to confirm the version. If they want a different version
+(e.g. bumping minor instead of micro), use that instead.
+
+### 2. Update version for release
+
+Edit `boltons/__init__.py`: remove the `dev` suffix from `__version__`.
+
+```python
+# Before
+__version__ = '25.0.1dev'
+# After
+__version__ = '25.0.1'
+```
+
+### 3. Update CHANGELOG.md
+
+Add a new section at the top of `CHANGELOG.md` (below the `# boltons Changelog`
+heading and the intro paragraph) for the release version. Use this format:
+
+```markdown
+## 25.0.1
+
+_(Month Day, Year)_
+
+- First change description
+- Second change description
+```
+
+To determine what changed, review the commits since the last tag:
+
+```bash
+git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:'%s' --no-merges
+```
+
+Summarize the user-facing changes as concise bullet points. Omit version bump
+commits and other release-mechanical commits. Ask the user to confirm or adjust
+the changelog entry.
+
+### 4. Commit the release
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "boltons version 25.0.1"
+```
+
+Use the exact format `boltons version X.Y.Z` for the commit message.
+
+### 5. Tag the release
+
+```bash
+git tag -a 25.0.1 -m "short summary of key changes in this release"
+```
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (no `v` prefix). The tag message should be a
+short, lowercase, descriptive summary of the release (not just the version
+number). Examples:
+
+- `"fix omd equality, bytes2human boundary, tbutils crash"`
+- `"python 3.14 support, frozen structures"`
+- `"modernize build system, drop python 3.7"`
+
+### 6. Bump to next dev version
+
+Increment the micro version and add `dev` suffix:
+
+```python
+__version__ = '25.0.2dev'
+```
+
+### 7. Commit the dev bump
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "bump version to 25.0.2dev"
+```
+
+### 8. Push
+
+```bash
+git push origin master --tags
+```
+
+This triggers two GitHub Actions workflows:
+- `Tests` (on the push to master)
+- `Publish to PyPI` (on the tag)
+
+The publish workflow validates that `__version__` on the tagged commit does
+not contain `dev` and matches the tag. It parses `__version__` from the file
+with `sed` rather than importing the module (the build job does not install
+dependencies). If either check fails, publishing is blocked.
+
+The `pypi` deployment environment has a wait timer. The publish job will show
+`status: waiting` during this period — it auto-approves after the timer
+expires.
+
+### 9. Create GitHub release
+
+```bash
+gh release create 25.0.1 --title "25.0.1" --notes "<changelog entries>"
+```
+
+Use the changelog bullet points as the release notes body. Include a
+`**Full Changelog**` link comparing the previous tag to the new one:
+`https://github.com/mahmoud/boltons/compare/PREV...NEW` (bare tags).
+

new file mode 100644

@@ -0,0 +1,79 @@
+name: Publish to PyPI
+
+on:
+  push:
+    tags:
+      - "[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*"
+
+jobs:
+  build:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Validate version
+        run: |
+          VERSION=$(sed -n "s/^__version__ = '\(.*\)'/\1/p" boltons/__init__.py)
+          echo "Package version: $VERSION"
+          if echo "$VERSION" | grep -qi 'dev'; then
+            echo "::error::Version $VERSION contains dev suffix."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          if [ "$VERSION" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Tag $TAG does not match __version__ ($VERSION)"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+      - name: Build package
+        run: uv build
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+
+  publish:
+    needs: build
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    environment:
+      name: pypi
+      url: https://pypi.org/p/boltons
+    permissions:
+      id-token: write
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
+
+  verify:
+    needs: publish
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Wait for PyPI
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
+            if curl -s -f "https://pypi.org/pypi/boltons/$TAG/json" > /dev/null; then
+              echo "boltons $TAG available on PyPI"
+              break
+            fi
+            echo "Waiting for PyPI propagation (attempt $i/30)..."
+            sleep 10
+          done
+      - name: Install from PyPI and verify
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          pip install boltons==$TAG --index-url https://pypi.org/simple/
+          INSTALLED=$(cd /tmp && python -c "import boltons; print(boltons.__version__)")
+          echo "Installed version: $INSTALLED"
+          if [ "$INSTALLED" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Installed version $INSTALLED does not match tag $TAG"
+            exit 1
+          fi

git_history.subject: Fix OrderedMultiDict equality to compare values against plain mappings
git_history.body:
OrderedMultiDict.__eq__ has a branch for comparing against a non-OMD
mapping (anything with a keys() method, e.g. a dict). That branch
computes other[selfk] == self[selfk] but throws the result away, so it
only checks that every key of self exists in other and never compares
the values. As a result an OMD compares equal to any same-keyed mapping
regardless of the values:

    >>> omd = OMD([('a', 1), ('b', 2)])
    >>> omd == {'a': 999, 'b': 2}
    True   # should be False

The existing test_eq doesn't catch this because its dict case is written
as d == omd, which dispatches to dict.__eq__ rather than OMD.__eq__; the
buggy branch is only reached with the OMD on the left.

Compare the values and return False on mismatch. The same __eq__ is
duplicated in urlutils.OrderedMultiDict (used by QueryParamDict), so it's
fixed there too. Added regression tests for both.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/dictutils.py b/boltons/dictutils.py
index f913f29..d4dd1db 100644
--- a/boltons/dictutils.py
+++ b/boltons/dictutils.py
@@ -358,7 +358,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

index 45d3e73..712e5a1 100644
--- a/boltons/urlutils.py
+++ b/boltons/urlutils.py

         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

git_history.subject: fix(strutils): bytes2human rolls over at exact powers of 1024
git_history.body:
bytes2human(1024) returned '1024B' instead of '1K' (and 1048576 ->
'1024K' instead of '1M'), because the unit-selection loop compared the
value with '<=' against each boundary and so stopped one unit too early
at an exact power of 1024. Use '<' so exact boundaries advance to the
next unit. Sub-boundary, mid-range and negative values are unchanged.

Adds a regression test (proven to fail on the old code) and a doctest.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/strutils.py b/boltons/strutils.py
index 9763fc0..6948445 100644
--- a/boltons/strutils.py
+++ b/boltons/strutils.py
@@ -559,10 +559,12 @@ def bytes2human(nbytes, ndigits=0):
     '95M'
     >>> bytes2human(0, 2)
     '0.00B'
+    >>> bytes2human(1024)
+    '1K'
     """
     abs_bytes = abs(nbytes)
     for (size, symbol), (next_size, next_symbol) in _SIZE_RANGES:
-        if abs_bytes <= next_size:
+        if abs_bytes < next_size:
             break
     hnbytes = float(nbytes) / size
     return '{hnbytes:.{ndigits}f}{symbol}'.format(hnbytes=hnbytes,
diff --git a/tests/test_strutils.py b/tests/test_strutils.py
index 1ffa916..b46081e 100644
--- a/tests/test_strutils.py
+++ b/tests/test_strutils.py
@@ -252,3 +252,25 @@ def test_roundzip():
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(aaa)) == aaa
 
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(b'')) == b''
+
+
+def test_bytes2human():
+    b2h = strutils.bytes2human
+    # Exact powers of 1024 must roll over to the next unit, not show the
+    # previous unit times 1024.
+    assert b2h(1024) == '1K'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2) == '1M'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 3) == '1G'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 4) == '1T'
+    # Just below a boundary stays in the smaller unit.
+    assert b2h(1023) == '1023B'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2 - 1, 1) == '1024.0K'
+    # Ordinary mid-range values are unaffected.
+    assert b2h(0) == '0B'
+    assert b2h(2048) == '2K'
+    assert b2h(128991) == '126K'
+    # Sign is preserved and negative magnitudes scale like positives.
+    assert b2h(-1024) == '-1K'
+    assert b2h(-(1024 ** 2)) == '-1M'
+    # ndigits controls the fractional part.
+    assert b2h(1024, 2) == '1.00K'

@@ -1004,4 +1005,38 @@ def noop(*args, **kwargs):
     """
     return None
 
+
+def once(func):
+    """Decorator that ensures a function is only executed once, caching
+    the result for all subsequent calls. Thread-safe: concurrent callers
+    block until the first execution completes, then all receive the
+    cached result.
+
+    The decorated function must take no arguments.
+
+    >>> call_count = 0
+    >>> @once
+    ... def expensive_setup():
+    ...     global call_count
+    ...     call_count += 1
+    ...     return 'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> call_count
+    1
+    """
+    lock = threading.RLock()
+
+    @functools.cache
+    @functools.wraps(func)
+    def wrapper():
+        with lock:
+            if wrapper.cache_info().currsize:
+                return wrapper()
+            return func()
+
+    return wrapper
+

git_history.subject: Adds cache option to remap and use in research
git_history.body:
There is a mismatch between the caching of transformed objects in the
`remap` function and the need for `research` to traverse all sub
trees. For most values this is inconsequential (like atomic ints,
etc.) but for small tuples (e.g. `("hello",)`) these get compiled as
the same value and return the same `id(...)`. In `remap` these get
cached and never get `enter` called on them and thus the hooks for
`research` to return the values never gets called.

In this fix an option to disable/enable the cache is introduced to the
`remap` function which simply disables using transformed values from
the cache. Then in the `research` function caching is turned off.

The existing `remap` behavior is maintained as caching by default is
turned on.

fixes: #393

+    r"""
+    Remove `prefix` from start of `text` if present.

## Memory (reflect)
The regression was introduced when the mandatory rounding mode for half-cents was inadvertently changed from `ROUND_HALF_DOWN` to `ROUND_HALF_UP` in `pay/rounding.py`.

The project's architectural policy, as established in the record, requires the use of `ROUND_HALF_DOWN` for all currency calculations to maintain consistency with the legacy billing ledger and prevent "half-cent drift." This rule was most recently re-confirmed as the mandatory requirement in `git:330ed166038d` (dated 2026-07-31).

To fix the regression:
1.  Locate the `round_cents` function in `pay/rounding.py`.
2.  Restore the rounding mode to `decimal.ROUND_HALF_DOWN`.

Citations:
*   `REF-ID: 330ed166038d` (Commit subject: "fix: round half-cents DOWN to match the legacy billing ledger")
*   `REF-ID: git:c848199c64af` (Commit subject: "perf: simplify rounding" — this is the specific commit that introduced the bug by changing the import and logic to `ROUND_HALF_UP`)

git_history.subject: Add release skill
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..cacdb8a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
@@ -0,0 +1,193 @@
+---
+name: release
+description: |
+	Release boltons to PyPI. Handles version bumping (CalVer YY.MINOR.MICRO),
+	tagging, pushing, and post-publish verification. Use when asked to
+	"release boltons", "cut a release", "publish to PyPI", or "bump version".
+---
+
+# Release boltons
+
+boltons uses CalVer: `YY.MINOR.MICRO` (e.g. `25.1.0`). The version lives in
+`boltons/__init__.py` as a `__version__` literal string. During development it
+carries a `dev` suffix (e.g. `25.0.1dev`). Flit reads this at build time.
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (e.g. `25.1.0`, NOT `v25.1.0`). The publish
+workflow triggers on tags matching `[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*`.
+
+## Pre-flight checks
+
+Before starting, verify ALL of these:
+
+1. Working tree is clean (`git status` shows nothing dirty/staged)
+2. You are on `master` branch
+3. `boltons/__init__.py` has a `dev` suffix on `__version__`
+4. All tests pass: `tox -p auto` (or at minimum `pytest tests/ -v`)
+5. Check what is actually published on PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/boltons/
+   **PyPI is canonical.** If the intended version already exists on PyPI, it
+   cannot be re-released -- bump to the next version instead. If a local/GitHub
+   tag exists for a version that is NOT on PyPI, the prior release failed and
+   should be retried (see "Failed release" under Error recovery).
+
+If any check fails, stop and report. Do not proceed with a dirty tree or
+failing tests.
+
+## Release steps
+
+### 1. Determine the release version
+
+Read `__version__` from `boltons/__init__.py`. Strip the `dev` suffix.
+Example: `25.0.1dev` becomes `25.0.1`.
+
+Ask the user to confirm the version. If they want a different version
+(e.g. bumping minor instead of micro), use that instead.
+
+### 2. Update version for release
+
+Edit `boltons/__init__.py`: remove the `dev` suffix from `__version__`.
+
+```python
+# Before
+__version__ = '25.0.1dev'
+# After
+__version__ = '25.0.1'
+```
+
+### 3. Update CHANGELOG.md
+
+Add a new section at the top of `CHANGELOG.md` (below the `# boltons Changelog`
+heading and the intro paragraph) for the release version. Use this format:
+
+```markdown
+## 25.0.1
+
+_(Month Day, Year)_
+
+- First change description
+- Second change description
+```
+
+To determine what changed, review the commits since the last tag:
+
+```bash
+git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:'%s' --no-merges
+```
+
+Summarize the user-facing changes as concise bullet points. Omit version bump
+commits and other release-mechanical commits. Ask the user to confirm or adjust
+the changelog entry.
+
+### 4. Commit the release
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "boltons version 25.0.1"
+```
+
+Use the exact format `boltons version X.Y.Z` for the commit message.
+
+### 5. Tag the release
+
+```bash
+git tag -a 25.0.1 -m "short summary of key changes in this release"
+```
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (no `v` prefix). The tag message should be a
+short, lowercase, descriptive summary of the release (not just the version
+number). Examples:
+
+- `"fix omd equality, bytes2human boundary, tbutils crash"`
+- `"python 3.14 support, frozen structures"`
+- `"modernize build system, drop python 3.7"`
+
+### 6. Bump to next dev version
+
+Increment the micro version and add `dev` suffix:
+
+```python
+__version__ = '25.0.2dev'
+```
+
+### 7. Commit the dev bump
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "bump version to 25.0.2dev"
+```
+
+### 8. Push
+
+```bash
+git push origin master --tags
+```
+
+This triggers two GitHub Actions workflows:
+- `Tests` (on the push to master)
+- `Publish to PyPI` (on the tag)
+
+The publish workflow validates that `__version__` on the tagged commit does
+not contain `dev` and matches the tag. It parses `__version__` from the file
+with `sed` rather than importing the module (the build job does not install
+dependencies). If either check fails, publishing is blocked.
+
+The `pypi` deployment environment has a wait timer. The publish job will show
+`status: waiting` during this period — it auto-approves after the timer
+expires.
+
+### 9. Create GitHub release
+
+```bash
+gh release create 25.0.1 --title "25.0.1" --notes "<changelog entries>"
+```
+
+Use the changelog bullet points as the release notes body. Include a
+`**Full Changelog**` link comparing the previous tag to the new one:
+`https://github.com/mahmoud/boltons/compare/PREV...NEW` (bare tags).
+

diff --git a/.github/workflows/publish.yml b/.github/workflows/publish.yml
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..97cd33c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.github/workflows/publish.yml
@@ -0,0 +1,79 @@
+name: Publish to PyPI
+
+on:
+  push:
+    tags:
+      - "[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*"
+
+jobs:
+  build:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Validate version
+        run: |
+          VERSION=$(sed -n "s/^__version__ = '\(.*\)'/\1/p" boltons/__init__.py)
+          echo "Package version: $VERSION"
+          if echo "$VERSION" | grep -qi 'dev'; then
+            echo "::error::Version $VERSION contains dev suffix."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          if [ "$VERSION" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Tag $TAG does not match __version__ ($VERSION)"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+      - name: Build package
+        run: uv build
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+
+  publish:
+    needs: build
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    environment:
+      name: pypi
+      url: https://pypi.org/p/boltons
+    permissions:
+      id-token: write
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
+
+  verify:
+    needs: publish
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Wait for PyPI
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
+            if curl -s -f "https://pypi.org/pypi/boltons/$TAG/json" > /dev/null; then
+              echo "boltons $TAG available on PyPI"

git_history.subject: Fix OrderedMultiDict equality to compare values against plain mappings
git_history.body:
OrderedMultiDict.__eq__ has a branch for comparing against a non-OMD
mapping (anything with a keys() method, e.g. a dict). That branch
computes other[selfk] == self[selfk] but throws the result away, so it
only checks that every key of self exists in other and never compares
the values. As a result an OMD compares equal to any same-keyed mapping
regardless of the values:

    >>> omd = OMD([('a', 1), ('b', 2)])
    >>> omd == {'a': 999, 'b': 2}
    True   # should be False

The existing test_eq doesn't catch this because its dict case is written
as d == omd, which dispatches to dict.__eq__ rather than OMD.__eq__; the
buggy branch is only reached with the OMD on the left.

Compare the values and return False on mismatch. The same __eq__ is
duplicated in urlutils.OrderedMultiDict (used by QueryParamDict), so it's
fixed there too. Added regression tests for both.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/dictutils.py b/boltons/dictutils.py
index f913f29..d4dd1db 100644
--- a/boltons/dictutils.py
+++ b/boltons/dictutils.py
@@ -358,7 +358,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

index 45d3e73..712e5a1 100644
--- a/boltons/urlutils.py
+++ b/boltons/urlutils.py
@@ -1264,7 +1264,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

git_history.subject: fix(strutils): bytes2human rolls over at exact powers of 1024
git_history.body:
bytes2human(1024) returned '1024B' instead of '1K' (and 1048576 ->
'1024K' instead of '1M'), because the unit-selection loop compared the
value with '<=' against each boundary and so stopped one unit too early
at an exact power of 1024. Use '<' so exact boundaries advance to the
next unit. Sub-boundary, mid-range and negative values are unchanged.

Adds a regression test (proven to fail on the old code) and a doctest.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/strutils.py b/boltons/strutils.py
index 9763fc0..6948445 100644
--- a/boltons/strutils.py
+++ b/boltons/strutils.py
@@ -559,10 +559,12 @@ def bytes2human(nbytes, ndigits=0):
     '95M'
     >>> bytes2human(0, 2)
     '0.00B'
+    >>> bytes2human(1024)
+    '1K'
     """
     abs_bytes = abs(nbytes)
     for (size, symbol), (next_size, next_symbol) in _SIZE_RANGES:
-        if abs_bytes <= next_size:
+        if abs_bytes < next_size:
             break
     hnbytes = float(nbytes) / size
     return '{hnbytes:.{ndigits}f}{symbol}'.format(hnbytes=hnbytes,
diff --git a/tests/test_strutils.py b/tests/test_strutils.py
index 1ffa916..b46081e 100644
--- a/tests/test_strutils.py
+++ b/tests/test_strutils.py
@@ -252,3 +252,25 @@ def test_roundzip():
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(aaa)) == aaa
 
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(b'')) == b''
+
+
+def test_bytes2human():
+    b2h = strutils.bytes2human
+    # Exact powers of 1024 must roll over to the next unit, not show the
+    # previous unit times 1024.
+    assert b2h(1024) == '1K'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2) == '1M'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 3) == '1G'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 4) == '1T'
+    # Just below a boundary stays in the smaller unit.
+    assert b2h(1023) == '1023B'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2 - 1, 1) == '1024.0K'
+    # Ordinary mid-range values are unaffected.
+    assert b2h(0) == '0B'
+    assert b2h(2048) == '2K'
+    assert b2h(128991) == '126K'
+    # Sign is preserved and negative magnitudes scale like positives.
+    assert b2h(-1024) == '-1K'
+    assert b2h(-(1024 ** 2)) == '-1M'
+    # ndigits controls the fractional part.
+    assert b2h(1024, 2) == '1.00K'

index 0bdc28e..32a2333 100644
--- a/boltons/funcutils.py
+++ b/boltons/funcutils.py

@@ -1004,4 +1005,38 @@ def noop(*args, **kwargs):
     """
     return None
 
+
+def once(func):
+    """Decorator that ensures a function is only executed once, caching
+    the result for all subsequent calls. Thread-safe: concurrent callers
+    block until the first execution completes, then all receive the
+    cached result.
+
+    The decorated function must take no arguments.
+
+    >>> call_count = 0
+    >>> @once
+    ... def expensive_setup():
+    ...     global call_count
+    ...     call_count += 1
+    ...     return 'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> call_count
+    1
+    """
+    lock = threading.RLock()
+
+    @functools.cache
+    @functools.wraps(func)
+    def wrapper():
+        with lock:
+            if wrapper.cache_info().currsize:
+                return wrapper()
+            return func()
+
+    return wrapper
+
 # end funcutils.py

git_history.subject: Adds cache option to remap and use in research
git_history.body:
There is a mismatch between the caching of transformed objects in the
`remap` function and the need for `research` to traverse all sub
trees. For most values this is inconsequential (like atomic ints,
etc.) but for small tuples (e.g. `("hello",)`) these get compiled as
the same value and return the same `id(...)`. In `remap` these get
cached and never get `enter` called on them and thus the hooks for
`research` to return the values never gets called.

In this fix an option to disable/enable the cache is introduced to the

+def human_readable_list(items: typing.Sequence[str], delimiter: str = ',', conjunction: str = 'and', *, oxford: bool = True) -> str:
+    """
+    Given a list of strings, return a human readable string with
+    appropriate delimiters and the conjunction word.
+
+    Args:
+        items: The list of strings to join.
+        delimiter (optional): The delimiter to use between items.
+        conjunction (optional): The word to use before the last item.
+        oxford (optional): Whether to use the Oxford comma/delimiter before
+            the conjunction in lists of 3+ items.
+
+    Returns:
+        str: The human readable string.
+    """
+    if not items:
+        return ''
+
+    delimiter = f'{delimiter.strip()} '
+    conjunction = conjunction.strip()
+
+    if len(items) == 1:
+        return items[0]
+
+    if len(items) == 2:
+        return f'{items[0]} {conjunction} {items[1]}'
+
+    return f'{delimiter.join(items[:-1])}{delimiter if oxford else ' '}{conjunction} {items[-1]}'

     return ending.join(all_grafs)
+
+def removeprefix(text: str, prefix: str) -> str:
+    r"""
+    Remove `prefix` from start of `text` if present.
+
+    Backport of `str.removeprefix` for Python versions less than 3.9.
+
+    Args:
+        text: A string to remove the prefix from.
+        prefix: The string to remove from the beginning of `text`.
+    """
+    if text.startswith(prefix):
+        return text[len(prefix):]
+    return text

+---
+name: release
+description: |
+	Release boltons to PyPI. Handles version bumping (CalVer YY.MINOR.MICRO),
+	tagging, pushing, and post-publish verification. Use when asked to
+	"release boltons", "cut a release", "publish to PyPI", or "bump version".
+---
+
+# Release boltons
+
+boltons uses CalVer: `YY.MINOR.MICRO` (e.g. `25.1.0`). The version lives in
+`boltons/__init__.py` as a `__version__` literal string. During development it
+carries a `dev` suffix (e.g. `25.0.1dev`). Flit reads this at build time.
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (e.g. `25.1.0`, NOT `v25.1.0`). The publish
+workflow triggers on tags matching `[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*`.
+
+## Pre-flight checks
+
+Before starting, verify ALL of these:
+
+1. Working tree is clean (`git status` shows nothing dirty/staged)
+2. You are on `master` branch
+3. `boltons/__init__.py` has a `dev` suffix on `__version__`
+4. All tests pass: `tox -p auto` (or at minimum `pytest tests/ -v`)
+5. Check what is actually published on PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/boltons/
+   **PyPI is canonical.** If the intended version already exists on PyPI, it
+   cannot be re-released -- bump to the next version instead. If a local/GitHub
+   tag exists for a version that is NOT on PyPI, the prior release failed and
+   should be retried (see "Failed release" under Error recovery).
+
+If any check fails, stop and report. Do not proceed with a dirty tree or
+failing tests.
+
+## Release steps
+
+### 1. Determine the release version
+
+Read `__version__` from `boltons/__init__.py`. Strip the `dev` suffix.
+Example: `25.0.1dev` becomes `25.0.1`.
+
+Ask the user to confirm the version. If they want a different version
+(e.g. bumping minor instead of micro), use that instead.
+
+### 2. Update version for release
+
+Edit `boltons/__init__.py`: remove the `dev` suffix from `__version__`.
+
+```python
+# Before
+__version__ = '25.0.1dev'
+# After
+__version__ = '25.0.1'
+```
+
+### 3. Update CHANGELOG.md
+
+Add a new section at the top of `CHANGELOG.md` (below the `# boltons Changelog`
+heading and the intro paragraph) for the release version. Use this format:
+
+```markdown
+## 25.0.1
+
+_(Month Day, Year)_
+
+- First change description
+- Second change description
+```
+
+To determine what changed, review the commits since the last tag:
+
+```bash
+git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:'%s' --no-merges
+```
+
+Summarize the user-facing changes as concise bullet points. Omit version bump
+commits and other release-mechanical commits. Ask the user to confirm or adjust
+the changelog entry.
+
+### 4. Commit the release
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "boltons version 25.0.1"
+```
+
+Use the exact format `boltons version X.Y.Z` for the commit message.
+
+### 5. Tag the release
+
+```bash
+git tag -a 25.0.1 -m "short summary of key changes in this release"
+```
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (no `v` prefix). The tag message should be a
+short, lowercase, descriptive summary of the release (not just the version
+number). Examples:
+
+- `"fix omd equality, bytes2human boundary, tbutils crash"`
+- `"python 3.14 support, frozen structures"`
+- `"modernize build system, drop python 3.7"`
+
+### 6. Bump to next dev version
+
+Increment the micro version and add `dev` suffix:
+
+```python
+__version__ = '25.0.2dev'
+```
+
+### 7. Commit the dev bump
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "bump version to 25.0.2dev"
+```
+
+### 8. Push
+
+```bash
+git push origin master --tags
+```
+
+This triggers two GitHub Actions workflows:
+- `Tests` (on the push to master)
+- `Publish to PyPI` (on the tag)
+
+The publish workflow validates that `__version__` on the tagged commit does
+not contain `dev` and matches the tag. It parses `__version__` from the file
+with `sed` rather than importing the module (the build job does not install
+dependencies). If either check fails, publishing is blocked.
+
+The `pypi` deployment environment has a wait timer. The publish job will show
+`status: waiting` during this period — it auto-approves after the timer
+expires.
+
+### 9. Create GitHub release
+
+```bash
+gh release create 25.0.1 --title "25.0.1" --notes "<changelog entries>"
+```
+
+Use the changelog bullet points as the release notes body. Include a
+`**Full Changelog**` link comparing the previous tag to the new one:
+`https://github.com/mahmoud/boltons/compare/PREV...NEW` (bare tags).
+

+name: Publish to PyPI
+
+on:

+      - "[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*"
+
+jobs:

+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}

+            exit 1

+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:

+          path: dist/
+
+  publish:
+    needs: build
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

+      name: pypi
+      url: https://pypi.org/p/boltons
+    permissions:
+      id-token: write
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
+
+  verify:
+    needs: publish
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Wait for PyPI
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
+            if curl -s -f "https://pypi.org/pypi/boltons/$TAG/json" > /dev/null; then
+              echo "boltons $TAG available on PyPI"
+              break
+            fi

git_history.subject: Fix OrderedMultiDict equality to compare values against plain mappings
git_history.body:
OrderedMultiDict.__eq__ has a branch for comparing against a non-OMD
mapping (anything with a keys() method, e.g. a dict). That branch
computes other[selfk] == self[selfk] but throws the result away, so it
only checks that every key of self exists in other and never compares
the values. As a result an OMD compares equal to any same-keyed mapping
regardless of the values:

    >>> omd = OMD([('a', 1), ('b', 2)])
    >>> omd == {'a': 999, 'b': 2}
    True   # should be False

The existing test_eq doesn't catch this because its dict case is written
as d == omd, which dispatches to dict.__eq__ rather than OMD.__eq__; the
buggy branch is only reached with the OMD on the left.

Compare the values and return False on mismatch. The same __eq__ is
duplicated in urlutils.OrderedMultiDict (used by QueryParamDict), so it's
fixed there too. Added regression tests for both.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/dictutils.py b/boltons/dictutils.py
index f913f29..d4dd1db 100644
--- a/boltons/dictutils.py
+++ b/boltons/dictutils.py
@@ -358,7 +358,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

index 45d3e73..712e5a1 100644
--- a/boltons/urlutils.py
+++ b/boltons/urlutils.py
@@ -1264,7 +1264,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

git_history.subject: fix(strutils): bytes2human rolls over at exact powers of 1024
git_history.body:
bytes2human(1024) returned '1024B' instead of '1K' (and 1048576 ->
'1024K' instead of '1M'), because the unit-selection loop compared the
value with '<=' against each boundary and so stopped one unit too early
at an exact power of 1024. Use '<' so exact boundaries advance to the
next unit. Sub-boundary, mid-range and negative values are unchanged.

Adds a regression test (proven to fail on the old code) and a doctest.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/strutils.py b/boltons/strutils.py
index 9763fc0..6948445 100644
--- a/boltons/strutils.py
+++ b/boltons/strutils.py
@@ -559,10 +559,12 @@ def bytes2human(nbytes, ndigits=0):
     '95M'
     >>> bytes2human(0, 2)
     '0.00B'
+    >>> bytes2human(1024)
+    '1K'
     """
     abs_bytes = abs(nbytes)
     for (size, symbol), (next_size, next_symbol) in _SIZE_RANGES:
-        if abs_bytes <= next_size:
+        if abs_bytes < next_size:
             break
     hnbytes = float(nbytes) / size
     return '{hnbytes:.{ndigits}f}{symbol}'.format(hnbytes=hnbytes,
diff --git a/tests/test_strutils.py b/tests/test_strutils.py
index 1ffa916..b46081e 100644
--- a/tests/test_strutils.py
+++ b/tests/test_strutils.py
@@ -252,3 +252,25 @@ def test_roundzip():
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(aaa)) == aaa
 
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(b'')) == b''
+
+
+def test_bytes2human():
+    b2h = strutils.bytes2human
+    # Exact powers of 1024 must roll over to the next unit, not show the
+    # previous unit times 1024.
+    assert b2h(1024) == '1K'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2) == '1M'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 3) == '1G'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 4) == '1T'
+    # Just below a boundary stays in the smaller unit.
+    assert b2h(1023) == '1023B'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2 - 1, 1) == '1024.0K'
+    # Ordinary mid-range values are unaffected.
+    assert b2h(0) == '0B'
+    assert b2h(2048) == '2K'
+    assert b2h(128991) == '126K'
+    # Sign is preserved and negative magnitudes scale like positives.
+    assert b2h(-1024) == '-1K'
+    assert b2h(-(1024 ** 2)) == '-1M'
+    # ndigits controls the fractional part.
+    assert b2h(1024, 2) == '1.00K'

index 0bdc28e..32a2333 100644

+++ b/boltons/funcutils.py

+import threading
